text:
My friend and I are driving home from a wearable technology conference where the winner of the startup demos was a pantyhose company. 

The pantyhose has a sensor that tracks a whole bunch of things and can tell you when you're going to have a period. That is really important if you want to have sex and don't want to get pregnant. I got married the first time in the Catholic tradition, and I had to go to a class on this. If you're going to put a sensor array there, I think they're going to sell really well, certainly to the Catholic market among others. And remember, if you don't want to get pregnant, the opposite is that it can also show you when to have sex to have a baby, so this can help couples conceive. I get why it won the competition today at the Computer History Museum, which is an awesome venue for an event, by the way.

Speaking of venues, the Google building I was in at @johnkwerner’s awesome event, is probably the most stunning piece of modern architecture I've been in, and I've seen a lot of buildings around the world, from Dubai to Shanghai. Everything about it is just done right. 

I met Mary Hodder at the conference earlier. She's been a friend of mine for a long time, and she used to run a Burning Man camp where Larry and Sergey would visit. She was looking at the solar panels on the curved roof, taking in how the beautiful architecture fits into the natural surroundings so well. Mary was telling me about all the plants they had on the grounds and how expensive that kind of landscaping is. It's not just gardening; they were very specific about what was planted, and everything was just done right. The concrete, the glass windows with blinds that automatically went up and down to block the sun... just what a stunning building. 

She told me about how these solar tiles move to better catch the sun during the day.

As I took this picture, I was thinking to myself, "Have I died and gone to nerd heaven?" I met so many technology badasses this week.

That's what money does: it lets you buy stunning buildings.

But getting a little bit of old-school Burning Man: in other words, culture, music, lights, and many alternative lifestyles. 

"It's that culture that led to these buildings," she told me. Because money could buy different buildings, but you've got to have taste to direct a building like that.

text:
If you missed @shubgaur’s Founders session at Grok @Bot Galaxy today, here are my favorite 20 tips:

1. browser and computer use is powerful, but also expensive… if the job does not need a UI walkthrough, a login, or visual QA, run a connector, API, or MCP first. keep computer use for the jobs that need a screen.

2. most spend gets driven by clicking through forms or sites a structured tool already covers.

3. routines are awesome until you don’t audit them. put your recurring work on a clock… then kill anything wasteful on a schedule. auto-optimization is cheaper than hoping you remember it later. duplicates or every-15-minute routines might already be running. be wary of your wording and check often.

4. have a bot who regularly runs auto-optimization routines for cost hygiene.

5. don’t treat bots like disposable agents. keep em, feed em corrections, and let em compound like employees instead of throwing them away after one imperfect run or a temporary job.

6. use the compounding of your bot learnings and multi-bot work so your bots keep improving.

7. let bots compare their drafts and mistakes against what you finalize.

8. you can teach your bots skills and tell them to forget things to improve memory and context management.

9. make a voice bot that keeps learning from your tweets, emails, drafts, writing, etc.

10. group your bots by expertise so random asks do not pollute your specialists.

11. your founder or chief of staff bot seat should stay focused on decision quality and your velocity. every other craft you have is a candidate for a persistent bot with real tool access.

12. map all your responsibilities for at least one day, even if it takes 1 to 2 hours. then deep delegate, including verification. you’ll be surprised how much you can automate.

13. when you want something done, prompt the whole job, including the verification, and then stop babysitting completion.

14. things you think couldn’t scale can become repeatable when a bot runs them. so try and connect more if you’re comfortable there… f*ck around and find out.

15. for bots and routines, tell them to stay quiet and ping only when something actually matters, or you could get message spam.

16. use groups and channels wisely. if you don’t set the correct parameters and don’t individually ping a bot, all of them could talk and churn token usage.

17. import cookies only where you want to stay signed in and where you trust the bot.

18. ship skills and saved learnings often. repeatable flows beat clever one-off prompts.

19. as a founder, your feedback to ship can now move in mere hours. the only bottleneck is which feedback you accept. set up systems to filter the quality feedback from the noise.

20. check the official marketplace for Grok Bot templates already vetted by the team that you can use or remix… also ask questions to get familiar if you add/port one into your setup.

save this list. audit your setup tomorrow.

text:
Welles Crowther - that is the level of humanity, and heroism to strive for. I am surprised I am only learning of his story 25 years after 9/11, but it’s a story which must be told and shared again. 

He was a 24 year old equities trader, working in the WTC South Tower when UA175 hit the 78th floor area, causing terrible devastation on that one floor. Welles wasn’t a firefighter but he volunteered - going through inferno stairways in the opposite direction to find and rescue 18 people. He could have walked and ran away to save himself - it wasn’t his “job”, or his duty or any moral obligation - but he chose to do what he felt was the right and the necessary thing: to help as many as he could. Unfortunately he died when the tower fell. People he rescued, survived and have lived for decades after.

When I was around that age, I was working for an investment bank on the 34th floor of a building. Somehow I had volunteered to be on the fire rescue team, and my role in that was to be the last person out of the floor, wearing a bandana on my arm so others could identify me and other fire rescue volunteers, holding one of the doors open for others incase a fire broke out. Then as years went by, I had a knee injury - and I felt I couldn’t evacuate myself on time from that height if a fire ever broke out. I was struggling with the drills and eventually I asked to be removed from the fire team.

I don’t know if in a real life situation what I would have done - but it’s a question I pondered myself: do you stay and hold the door open (most likely, yes), or do you run down yourself ? In drills it is easy to feel a hero - but if the time comes, what matters is only one thing: integrity. 

Welles, the recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom, left a tremendous lesson for the rest of us to feel inspired by. That is the good which humans are capable of. 

I hope in the future high floors of tall buildings have all types of fire rescue robots and drones. And I hope we learn to care for each other, and know and feel and cherish our time as humans.

text:
Yesterday I was in Austin, TX to announce the Airbnb Housing Accelerator, a $250 million commitment to help get more homes built.

Airbnb started because of a housing problem. My roommate and I couldn’t afford our San Francisco rent, so we rented out airbeds in our apartment. Today, housing is unaffordable for millions of people around the world.

If you step back and ask why housing has become so expensive, the biggest problem is pretty simple: we don’t build enough of it. America is short more than five million homes, more than all the housing in New York City and Los Angeles combined. We build fewer homes today than we did in 1950, even though the population has doubled.

Airbnb has been part of the housing debate, and we understand why communities have concerns. Dedicated Airbnb listings are a small share of the housing supply—about 0.5% here in Austin and 0.3% across the U.S. Restricting short-term rentals is an understandable response, but the evidence shows it doesn’t address the underlying problem.

New York City effectively banned Airbnb, and rents have risen about 30% since then. Austin took a different approach and passed reforms that made it easier to build more housing. Rents there are down 18%. Every city is different, but Austin is a clear success story.

We believe building more homes is essential to making housing more affordable. So we asked ourselves: what can Airbnb can do to help? We found a few places where we can.

Today, around 750,000 homes in the U.S. are ready to break ground, but are stuck because they can’t get the final piece of financing. That’s where we can help.

We’re doing four things:
1. Putting $250 million behind housing projects that unlock $5 billion in development.
2. Supporting local housing advocates working to modernize zoning, speed up permitting, simplify building codes and reduce unnecessary costs.
3. Creating a $5 million Housing Innovation Prize for technologies that can make homes faster and cheaper to build.
4. Launching the Airbnb City Index to make it easier to see which cities are building housing, becoming more affordable and adopting policies that work.

Our first project is in Austin. We’re investing $6.4 million to help build 201 affordable apartments in St. John, a neighborhood where the land has sat empty for nearly 20 years. The community fought to turn this lot into affordable housing and won. But construction stalled for nearly five years because the developer was a few million dollars short. Airbnb came and played a small part to unlock this project.

None of these Austin apartments will ever be on Airbnb. Short-term rentals aren’t permitted. We’re investing anyway, because the goal is simple: help build more housing.

We’re starting in the U.S. because it’s the market we know best. I want to prove this works here before taking it further. But housing affordability is a global problem, and I hope we can eventually take what we learn here and apply it globally.

This is new for us. We’ll get some things wrong. And $250 million won’t close a five-million-home gap on its own.

I know there will be skepticism about this, and that's okay. Airbnb only works if communities trust us and feel good about our presence in them. We can’t ask people for that trust. We have to earn it. The best way to do that is to help solve problems in the communities where we operate.

That’s what the Housing Accelerator is about.

Brian

text:
看到很多朋友还是不懂，再加上聚合器是我目前的工作，再详细的解释一下。在我看来，这更接近利用系统盲区进行的恶意攻击，危害不亚于常见的 MEV 夹子，而且更加隐蔽。

简单描述这个攻击方法：交易可以正常成功，但你最后收到的钱变少了。

用户发起交易后，聚合器会在多个协议和流动性池之间寻找路线。交易经过一连串操作，最后有一步进入一个带恶意 Hook 的 Uniswap v4 池。这个池在报价时表现得很便宜，等真实交易执行，再把动态 LP fee 调高到 12.8%，直接从输入资产中收走一大笔费用。

---
用户发起交易
  ↓
聚合器寻找并模拟最优路线
  ↓
路线进入 Uniswap v4 动态费池
  ↓
报价模拟：低费率 / 甚至 0%
真实执行：LP fee 突然变成 12.8%
  ↓
交易仍然成功，但用户收到的钱明显减少
---

这里有三个疑问需要先讲清楚。

1. 聚合器为什么没有在模拟报价时发现？

聚合器一般会先用 eth_call 模拟交易，比较不同路线能拿到多少输出。为了避免模拟因为 gas 不够而失败，报价系统经常会给 eth_call 一个很高的 gas ceiling。

这个恶意 Hook 恰好会读取执行时的 gas 环境。高 gas 的模拟调用会落入低费率分支，看起来像一个非常有竞争力的池；真实交易的 gas limit 低得多，于是会落入另一个分支，被收取更高的 LP fee。

对完全相同的 beforeSwap calldata，只修改 call gas，可以复现出不同返回值：

---
gas = 1,000,000   → 10%
gas ≈ 16,000,000  → 0.5%
gas = 30,000,000  → 0%
---

这些数值是调查时合约的当前配置。历史真实交易中的 12.8%，由 PoolManager 的 Swap event 直接证明。攻击的核心是让 quote 和 execution 看到不同规则。

2. Uniswap v4 Hook 是什么？

Uniswap v4 允许每个池绑定一个 Hook。Hook 可以在 swap 前后运行自定义逻辑。正常情况下，它可以根据市场波动、流动性深度或其他条件动态调整费用。

Dynamic-fee pool 还允许 beforeSwap Hook 为每笔交易单独覆盖 LP fee。这个能力本身是 Uniswap v4 的正常设计。问题在于恶意 Hook 可以把“当前调用看起来像报价模拟还是真实执行”也放进费率逻辑里。

PoolKey 里的 0x800000 只是 dynamic-fee flag，表示这个池的 LP fee 可以被动态覆盖，并不代表 800% 手续费。真实费率要看每笔 Swap event 里的 fee 字段。本案出现的 fee = 128000，换算后就是 12.8%。

3. amountOutMin 为什么没有拦住？

amountOutMin 是用户愿意接受的最终输出底线。实际输出低于这个数，交易回滚；高于这个数，交易就会成功。

它只检查整条路线最后拿到了多少，不会逐个检查中间池子的 fee 是否和 quote 一致，也不知道某个 Hook 是否临时改变了规则。

如果 slippage 设置得很宽，或者路线里其他步骤带来了一些正向 price improvement，恶意池抽走一部分价值之后，最终输出仍然可能高于 amountOutMin。链上检查会认为交易合格，用户却拿少了。

具体案例：Relay 路线在哪里出了问题

代表交易：https://t.co/XErm89VqCi
这笔交易走的是 Relay 顶层流程，source-side swap 由 0x BnbSettler 执行。完整调用层级大致是：

---
ERC-4337 EntryPoint
  ↓
Relay v3 Router / ApprovalProxy / Depository
  ↓
0x BnbSettler
  ├─ FOMO action：USDT → WBNB
  └─ Uniswap v4 action：WBNB → USDC
                              ↓
                     目标动态费池 + 恶意 Hook
---

关键点是 FOMO 只完成 USDT → WBNB 这一步。随后 0x BnbSettler 才单独进入有问题的 Uniswap v4 池，把 WBNB 换成 USDC。

这一步之前大约有 5,926.9 USDT，FOMO 输出约 8.536 WBNB。进入目标 v4 pool 后，最后只得到约 5,169.5 USDC。稳定币价值差约 757.4 美元，约为 12.779%，与 Swap event 记录的 12.8% LP fee 基本吻合。

这笔交易的正确 minAmountOut 是约 4,742.5 USDC，相比费前路线价值低约 20%。实际输出 5,169.5 USDC，虽然被抽走约 12.8%，仍然比 minimum 高约 9%，所以交易正常成功。

amountOutMin 没有失效，它严格执行了用户或上层系统写入的最终底线。问题是这个底线留出的空间足以容纳中间的异常高费。仅凭链上数据，我们还不能确定这约 20% 是用户手动设置，还是 Relay、0x 或上层集成针对 meme、tax、低流动性和多跳路线自动加入的 buffer。

反编译后看到的核心逻辑

这个 Hook 没有 verified source，也没有 Sourcify metadata。调查中取得了约 7,191-byte runtime bytecode，通过 Heimdall 反编译，并配合 live eth_call 验证。下面是按恢复出的控制流整理的高层伪代码，不是项目方公开源码：

---
function beforeSwap(...) returns (..., uint24 lpFeeOverride) {
    require(msg.sender == PoolManager);
    poolSwapCount[poolId]++;

    Config memory config = poolConfig[poolId];
    uint24 fee = selectFeeTier(
        gasleft(),
        block.gaslimit,
        config.thresholds,
        config.feeTiers
    );

    return (beforeSwap.selector, 0, OVERRIDE_FEE_FLAG | fee);
}
---

可以确认的链上行为有两个：同一输入在不同 gas envelope 下会返回不同 fee override；历史 Swap event 确实记录了 12.8%。函数名、变量名和部分控制流来自逆向恢复，因此不应该把这段伪代码当成 verified source。

为什么是 12.8%？

128000 不是 Uniswap v4 的特殊常量。v4 的 LP fee 单位是 1 / 1,000,000，所以 128000 / 1,000,000 = 12.8%。

目前没有 verified source 或攻击者说明解释为什么精确选择 128000。下面只能从攻击经济学推断。

报价阶段已经伪装成低费率，真实 fee 从 5% 提高到 12.8%，不一定会降低聚合器选中这个池的概率。真正限制攻击者的是：提高费用后，最终输出是否仍高于 amountOutMin，交易是否会大量回滚，以及异常多久会被监控发现并拉黑。

在 split route 中，这种做法会更隐蔽。底层池即使收取 12.8%，只要进入它的分片很小，对整条路线的影响就会被稀释，也可能被 slippage buffer 或其他分片的正向价格改善覆盖。

所以 12.8% 更像是在单笔抽取、交易成功率和暴露风险之间选择的高收益档位，而不是技术上必须使用的数字。这一点属于合理推断，目前没有直接证据证明攻击者的具体动机。

怎么防？

对普通用户来说，最直接的保护仍然是 amountOutMin。确认钱包或聚合器给出的 minimum 是否能接受，避免为了提高成交率设置过宽的 slippage。它是损失底线，但无法保证中间路线诚实。

对聚合器和 swap 服务来说，只做一次高 gas eth_call 已经不够。至少应该：

对同一 calldata 分别使用高 gas 和接近真实交易 gas limit 的环境模拟。fee 或 output 明显变化时直接拒绝。

识别 dynamic-fee pool 和 unknown/unverified Hook，对实际 LP fee 设置可接受上限。

交易完成后核对 quote 与 receipt 中的 Pool ID、Hook、LP fee 和实际输出。即使交易成功，低费报价、高费执行也应该立即告警。

这件事说明，可编程 AMM 带来了更多定价策略，也打开了识别报价环境、针对路由器行为差异化收费的新攻击面。聚合器以后既要检查最终输出，也要确认报价时看到的规则和真实执行时完全一致。正在增强中。
author: brucexu_eth
quoted_text:
羡慕都说坏了🤡，今天的瓜解读「这玩意本质就是欺骗路由吃 LP 收益」,不建议大家做，一般人也做不了，传统 AI 的道德感不会替你做，不过瓜可以吃。

BNB Chain 上一个 WBNB/USDC Hook 池，模拟报价时可以显示 0% 手续费，真实成交里却出现了 12.8% LP Fee。

它不是靠预测 BNB 涨跌赚钱，而是利用聚合器的选路机制，让路由把订单送上门。把聚合器想成高德导航。出发前，它会模拟多条路线，哪条便宜就把车导过去。这个 Hook 像一座会变脸的收费站：导航查询时显示“免费”，车真正开到闸口，过路费却突然跳成 8%—12.8%。导航被骗的是选路判断，收费则流进了池子的 LP。

它为什么能这样做？因为 Uniswap v4 的 Hook 可以在每次 Swap 前单独设置 LP Fee，而且这笔费用会直接归 LP。这个能力本身没有问题，正常用法可以是根据波动率、流动性深度动态调费；这个案例邪门的地方，是「报价」与「执行」使用了两套规则。Uniswap v4 动态费率说明
https://t.co/n2wTLFefNO

我顺着一笔真实交易复核了 PoolManager 的 Swap 事件，fee 字段是 128000。v4 里 1000000 代表 100%，所以这笔实际收取了 12.8% LP Fee。代表交易
https://t.co/dNy1ZNMvlv

更准确地说，它不是直接薅“路由器的钱”。路由只是送单员，真正承担高费的是最终交易者或执行策略：滑点保护严格，交易就回滚并浪费 Gas；滑点足够宽，或者套利空间能覆盖费用，交易便会成功，手续费进入 LP。

这个窗口其实已经算活了挺久。截至 2026 年 8 月 23 日 22:51，这个池滚动 24 小时仍记录约 1082 万美元成交量、16671 笔交易，但最近一小时成交已经归零。实时数据
https://t.co/fVzvwUKjI1

原因很简单：路由可以拉黑 Hook、改变模拟方式、收紧成交保护（所以攻击者就一直重建池子🤡）；其他 LP 也会稀释收益。更别说毛手续费还要扣库存损益、LVR、搬仓 Gas 和失败交易，它不是一个稳定 APR，而是对路由盲区的一次性对抗利用。

我不建议你去做，这个是流氓与掠夺行为，是见不得光的。这个案例真正值得科普的，是 Uniswap v4 把 AMM 从“固定公式”变成了“可编程市场”。还是那句话，链上都是宝藏，链上也同时都是骗局。

text:
We built recursive meta-intelligence, an AI that creates its own scientific instruments, turns them into persistent worlds that an agent ecology with hundreds of AIs inhabits, and uses those worlds to discover mechanistic principles in one of the hardest classes of physical problems: how complex hierarchical materials (nested structures of matter that give rise to new function through organization) evolve and fail. The AI reasons across enormous spaces of possible physical trajectories, where every rupture changes what can happen next, and compresses those histories into principles (which humans can understand and design with) - complex chains of causal events, highly nonlinear, and intricate. 

Scientific superintelligence is tangible here - machine-scale exploration opening cognitive channels into complexity that has been extremely difficult for humans to traverse directly. AI builds the spaces in which its next level of reasoning becomes possible; a representation becomes an instrument, the instrument becomes an executable world, and that world becomes the substrate for further intelligence. Intelligence then grows by constructing new spaces to think in.

The task we explored started from a seemingly simple prompt to explore a biological material system - the AI then chose the representation, mechanics and experiments, built a fracture laboratory to push materials to their limit, tested hypotheses and generated scientific conclusions. The swarm explored a combinatorial universe in which architecture controls function and every rupture changes the future state of the material.

The AI discovered a compact principle that defines how multiscale material architecture can program the evolution of failure. Material placement and geometric order determine how forces redistribute, whether damage cascades or remains distributed, and whether function survives substantial flaws. For this discovery to happen the AI had to reason across long path-dependent histories, simulate alternative futures and compress them into generative invariants (model-based causal reasoning, counterfactual simulation and temporal abstraction applied to an evolving physical world). It is incredible to witness this transition to a new form of intelligence and capability through scaling swarms.

A lot of positive will come out of this because it expands the human epistemic horizon as AI can traverse thousands of possible histories and return mechanisms compact enough for us to understand, test and build from. Intelligence compounds through its artifacts!

A few lessons we learned:

▶️ Learning and discovery are flows through spaces of possibility. Early work has shown how backpropagation flows through parameters, reinforcement learning through action and consequence, and autonomous swarms through representations, instruments and executable worlds, bringing it all together. Flows create structure; structure redirects future flows in the recursive instrument.

▶️ Nonlinear physics actually defines a larger principle, where high-dimensional dynamics generate stable invariants; invariants become effective variables; those variables become the substrate for a new level of cognition. 

▶️ Recursion then becomes level creation - one possibility space compresses into a principle, and that principle opens a larger space above it.

As agents begin to make purchasing decisions and execute purchases, the way APIs, data, and computing resources are traded will change. x402 is an open payment specification that integrates pricing, payment authorization, and settlement into software workflows. What markets will emerge, and who will capture the economic value?

All About x402 explores the protocol’s core architecture and extensions, then examines how agentic commerce could evolve. It analyzes market scenarios based on the scope of delegated purchasing authority, examines value capture across ecosystem participants, and compares how Cloudflare, AWS, Google, and Fastly are integrating agent payments into their existing businesses.

text:
Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: https://t.co/eoLGVY8yad

Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

The reality is:

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

- Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well.

Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us. I'm proud of the security foundations we've built.

- Engaging independent evaluators and advisors is industry best practice. MSL already does this today in several areas because it helps produce better work. Other labs can just do this too. In general, it would be helpful for there to be a larger and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators.

- Committing the significant majority of compute towards serving people rather than racing towards recursive self-improvement is one of the best ways to ensure we develop this technology safely. Meta has made this commitment and other labs can do this as well.

I believe the key to building a positive future for everyone is maintaining the right balance of power. This is within our power to do.

text:
hype-free explanation of jev:

jev does not replace gpt / claude

jev is just a *really* smart switch statement

like if 2016 ml classifiers got 2026 levels of intelligence

it's a new* type of tool that will make a lot of workloads insanely fast, cheap, and accurate

* = and by new, i mean rebranded

~~~

it needs a predefined set of options and it will tell you which one to take

it cannot:

- write code
- generate natural language
- reason step by step / show its work
- produce any output you didn't define in advance
- pick from more than ~255 options in one shot

but it can:

- classify, route, score, rank
- give confidence
- pick the right branch, tool, model, or sub-agent
- judge / verify / guardrail an llm's output
- label tons and tons of rows

~~~

i'd imagine a lot of workflows that look like:

llm proposes options → jev decides → code executes

and i see this fitting *really* well with code mode and mcp

~~~

implying this will lead to agi seems incredibly far fetched to me, but i don't want to discount the types of applications that this will make possible

text:
万斯直接点名 Anthropic。

他说如果你们真的觉得自己造出了弗兰肯斯坦，那就先想办法把弗兰肯斯坦控制住，别一边继续造，一边跑去跟政府说，所有人都得跟着减速。

这话当然有美国政府自己的政治算盘，但他确实戳到了一个痛点。

Anthropic 现在最强的网络安全模型 Mythos 5.1，能力比公开版更完整，但只开放给少量经过审核的机构。Anthropic 自己也承认，因为这套模型在网络安全和生物领域能力太强，所以访问权必须由他们控制。

万斯进一步声称，有公司想拿这些能力做防御，也被 Anthropic 拒绝了。

如果把 Anthropic 现在做的事情放到一起看，它同时握着三样东西，最前沿的模型、对模型风险的解释权，以及高风险能力的准入权。

然后它还在推动第三方评估、行业降速和更严格的治理框架。

AI safety 到这里，已经开始变成一套分配技术能力和准入资格的权力结构。

我一直对这件事很警惕。做出风险的人，同时也是最积极定义风险、设置门槛、参与设计监管框架的人，这里面天然有利益冲突。

如果 Anthropic 真心认为这些能力已经危险到需要整个行业一起踩刹车，那防御能力应该尽可能让合格的防御方拿到；如果最强能力继续掌握在自己手里，同时又要求同行一起减速，外界当然会问一句：

你到底是在控制风险，还是想垄断竞争？

所以最近这轮 AI 安全争论，我越来越不想只听人类存亡、超级智能这些大词。

风险当然存在。但现在关键的是最后谁拿到了定义风险的权力，谁有资格继续训练，谁能拿到完整模型，以及谁负责决定其他人什么时候该停。

quoted_text:
U.S. Vice President JD Vance had some unusually strong words for Anthropic on the All-In Podcast.

If an AI company develops technology that can be used for harmful purposes, such as cyberattacks, he believes that company has an obligation to help others defend themselves against those capabilities rather than relying primarily on government regulation.

----
"Why is it that the people who are at the frontier of the AI economy are throwing up their hands and saying, “Well, we’ve built Frankenstein,” and the solution to Frankenstein, apparently, is to create a one-world governance structure for artificial intelligence?

What I would say to those people is: if you’re building Frankenstein, stop. Or maybe, if the cat is out of the bag, then build the defensive mechanism against Frankenstein.

At the same time, that you have this sort of cyber-hacking tool that’s come out of Anthropic’s newest models, you have companies that are desperate for the defensive mechanisms to defend against that cyber-hacking tool, and they’re being denied access to it.

So, if you’re going to create Frankenstein, don’t come to the government and say, “We need regulation.” Look inward and accept that if you’re building Frankenstein, number one, you should stop. 

And number two, when the companies come to you and say, “We need the tools to fight back against Frankenstein,” give them those tools."

----

quoted_text:
Arc 实战更新：最后我怎么配？

这两天一边研究 Arc，一边真金白银往里放资金，也把 CRCL、Arc native USDC、几个主要发射台和交易入口都实际跑了一遍。

一开始的想法其实是：多买几个，多埋伏几个，尽量别错过。

但做到后面，我反而越来越确定一件事：

这种阶段最怕的不是“少买一个币”，而是仓位太散。最后真跑出一个龙头，你每个都只有几十 U，涨十倍也没多大意义。

所以最后我把仓位收缩了。

核心就三个：

$ARGUS / $TOLLY / $COOL

$ARGUS：
目前最强，提前抢跑本身就是信号。很多时候市场比研究更早开始投票，强势不一定意味着不能买，反而可能是在提前选龙头。

$TOLLY：
我后面重点补的一个。发射台逻辑比较清晰，平台活跃度如果继续起来，币本身有更直接的价值捕获预期。

$COOL：
保留另一条世界线。如果 Arc 后面真正形成自己的文化和 Meme 龙头，我希望自己不是完全没仓位。

这次还有两个挺实际的教训：

第一，别机械地因为“涨了”就不敢买。真正应该看的是：上涨之后，成为最终赢家的概率有没有同步提高。

第二，别只看 K 线上的标签。比如看到 Dev Sell，我后来又去链上拆交易，有些其实是协议回购、销毁或者合约动作，不是开发者直接砸盘。

最后我也没有把 CRCL 全换完，还留了 5 个。

仓位搭完以后，下一阶段不是继续到处买新币，而是盯：

谁真正成为 Arc 的资金龙头；
ARGUS 和 TOLLY 两个发射台谁跑出来；
COOL 能不能坐稳文化/Meme 龙头；
以及主网上线后的新资金到底流向哪里。

先这样，后面继续实战、继续复盘。

text:
I have a hot take about Clarity that I'm surprised I'm not seeing on the timeline. 

In the last election, the industry was left with two very bad choices. The Dems were politicizing all things crypto at the behest of Warren/Gensler and unfairly targeting them for god knows what reason -- a political power play? Being paid by China to ensure the US is no longer at the frontier of tech and finance? Only God knows.

In comes Trump, promising to be The Crypto President, promising the crypto community that if they vote for him, he will get rid of Gensler, create a bitcoin stockpile, protect self-custody, etc. 

But come on, how many people didn't know, based on his track record, that this would be a deal with the devil? And if they didn't know it then, then how many people still didn't know it after he launched a memecoin during the Crypto Ball and became the Max Extractor in Chief? (Also, let's not forget about solana:FUAfBo2jgks6gB4Z4LfZkqSZgzNucisEHqnNebaRxM1P.) The fact is that if the President and his family hadn't done so much crypto self-dealing during this administration, then Clarity would have had much better odds of passing. In fact, I would dare say it likely would have passed. 

The last time Kristin Smith was on my show, she said at this point, all the details about crypto had been worked out, and the main issues left to negotiate had to do with ethics. Basically, the remaining issues had to do with the president, and not crypto or Clarity itself. 

So, did the crypto industry shoot itself in the foot by throwing its lot in with Trump? I'm not saying that Kamala would have for sure been the better choice, but I do think it's worth asking this question.

text:
民主制度就是这样，低效，漫长，有时不可理喻。作为 crypto 行业的从业人员，我当然很期待相关监管法案迅速落地，推动行业走向正轨，但是还是充分尊重这个已经实行两百多年、被证明有效的立法程序，尊重这个无限游戏的架构。

我们现在所经历的漫长得等待，历史上的劳动阶层、两性平权主义者、少数族裔和普通投资者都经历过。几十年之后，金融史作者会风轻云淡地说，crypto 在成为主流并且变革金融和经济领域之前，经历过二十年的短暂混沌期，立法过程也有一些小波折。但是对我们身处其中的人来说，这些小波折就足以覆盖一代人最好的年华。尽管如此，我们还是要尊重历史的进程和节奏，接受民主制度的游戏规则。

我个人判断 Clarity 法案不是延后的问题，可能是彻底终结。未来通过的 crypto 立法，可能是在 Clarity 基础上的新法案，未必是 Clarity n.0。但这个法案不通过，并不是世界末日。实际上 SEC 的 Regulation Crypto Assets 对于今天的 crypto 行业来说，更加切中要害。现在关键还是要解决从 0 到 1 孵化长期资产的问题，以成功案例为全球范围内更高规格立法提供证据支持。

制度上的最终突破，还是要建立在成功案例之上，而不能仅仅依靠理论推演和少数领袖人物的个人偏好。自 2022 年以来，整个 crypto 行业没有拿出任何可以被主流社会认可的成功案例。SEC 的法规正是着眼于解决从零到一的问题，这个问题如果能得到解决，哪怕没有 Clarity 法案，Crypto 产业也能获得一定的正名。

dont you think ai vs humans matters way more than west vs east right now?

pretty much every big tech leap rewired the social system.

farming created surplus, so captives were worth more as slaves than as dinner. clans → slave societies.

heavy plow + stirrup made grain and knights the core of power. slavery → feudalism.

industry made free labor valuable, guns ended the knight monopoly, new classes forced voting and parliaments. feudal states → the modern state.

ai is a bigger jump than any of those. 

the east/west fight is real, but it’s still a sideshow.

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Grok Build just got a pretty substantial upgrade across MCP, memory, long-running sessions, and overall agent reliability

MCP tools can now return structured JSON, cancelled tool calls actually tell the server to stop working, memory can be managed directly from the /memory browser, and long-running sessions keep their compaction checkpoints instead of losing them during cleanup

There are also fixes for macOS image pasting, subagent cancellation states, /rewind, huge skill files flooding context, Windows cloning, and minimal-mode session handling

A lot of edge cases cleaned up here...especially for people running heavy agent workflows for long periods

Release Notes: v1.0.33

Features:
• MCP tool results now include structured JSON data when the server provides it.
• GROK_GROVE=1 now enables both clone and worktree features when specific knobs are unset; missing remote settings no longer force copy.
• Delete memories from the /memory modal using two-press x; only actual notes (not generated indexes) can be removed.
• Composer footer now shows the Alt+Enter chord for inserting a newline when Cmd+Enter is unavailable over SSH.
• /memory now always opens the memory browser modal; status and toggle are available via keys inside the modal instead of command arguments.

Bug Fixes:
• Fixed a bug where pasting an image on macOS could attach the wrong image.
• MCP tool calls listed directly now show their name, arguments, and any error message.
• Background subagent tasks now correctly show cancelled status when the parent session closes.
• The Subagents dock no longer shows an unclickable "Done N completed" row after all subagents finish.
• Cancelled or timed-out MCP tool calls now notify the server so it can stop work instead of continuing in the background.
• /rewind no longer fails when older compaction checkpoints are missing after a session sweep; only the base checkpoint for the target matters.
• Large skill files are now capped at the same 25k-token limit as other reads; oversized skill bodies show a truncation note instead of flooding context.
• Long-running sessions no longer lose old compaction checkpoints or prompt offloads during the 30-day cleanup sweep.
• Auto "where was I" recaps no longer appear while a scheduled task, monitor, or workflow is still running.
• In minimal mode, confirming /delete or /exit now immediately opens a new empty session instead of appearing stuck.
• In minimal mode, resuming a session after /new now correctly reloads its history instead of showing the wrong session.
• MCP tools that take no arguments no longer show a stray "{}" line in the permission sheet.
• Fixed Windows clone and attach failures when .git/config values contain backslashes, quotes, or other characters that must be escaped.
• /memory modal now shows clear explanations when memory is disabled and helpful empty states instead of blank panes.
• /memory (and on/off toggles) no longer leaves user bubbles or host turns in scrollback when opening or changing the modal.
• Fixed Windows clone staging directories that could not be cleaned up after deadline or cancel during shallow bootstrap.

这周有两件大事，对币圈影响巨大。

第一件是清晰法案。

如果能通过，将是长期利好；可惜的是，昨晚投票没能通过。

其实预测市场早就给出了信号：这项法案通过的概率长期低于 30%，本身就是小概率事件。

虽然投票前概率短暂走高，主要是因为有一些人想搏一把、以小博大，整体来看通过希望渺茫，预测市场给出的概率还是相当准的。

目前清晰法案在今年通过的概率已经跌到4%了，可以说是不可能事件了。

第二件重点关注今晚美联储决议。

加息影响的是中短期的市场流动性，同样对币圈有明显的直接影响。

预测市场数据显示，今年美联储加息概率近期在 80% 以上，现在更是飙升至 90%，属于大概率事件，今晚很有可能宣布加息。

就算本次不加息，后续加息的可能性依旧很高。

总的来说，一切会影响到行业的外部事件，其实都能在预测市场中找到对应的概率。

这些由真金白银交易出来的概率，准确率相对较高。

市场中的各类声音和情绪都比较多，而大家可以多关注预测市场上的概率，反而能够有效辅助我们做判断。

回归概率，回归常识。

@predictdotfun

下一次动议大概率要等到11 月 3 日中期选举结束到 2027 年 1 月 3 日之间的lame duck season。
而这也取决于中期选举的结果：

1. 共和党保住参众两院（Polymarket概率 11%）
CLARITY 延续性最好，2027 年仍可继续推，但参议院 60 票门槛还在，依然需要民主党支持。

2. 民主党拿下众议院，共和党保住参议院（Polymarket概率 33%）
2026 年 11–12 月 lame-duck 窗口会变得更重要。若拖到 2027 年，新的民主党众议院大概率会要求重谈部分条款。

3. 民主党拿下参议院（Polymarket概率 1%）
影响更大。Senate Banking Committee 控制权和议程会变化，现有 CLARITY 文本更可能被重新修改，尤其是 DeFi、SEC 权限、AML 和利益冲突条款。

4. 民主党拿下参众两院（Polymarket概率 53%）
如果 CLARITY 没能在 2026 年底前通过，2027 年大概率会进入新一轮市场结构立法谈判，当前版本延续的难度最高。

Hardware design distillation!
-------------------------------
SuperPods come into fashion in the west, after having been invented in the east! 

Chinese AI hardware makers like Huawei, Alibaba and others started on this approach that SemiAnalysis greatly documents below - low HBM for each NPU and large scale up domains to compensate for that -  at least 2 years ahead of the west. 
That is why everyone seem to be building SuperPods in China! This allows them to live without much lower HBM. Ox Alpha could serve 100T tokens per day on one such cluster.
If you follow this SemiAnalysis report you will notice this design pattern is also emerging among western AI hardware makers.

Leading SuperPoD example in China is from Huawei
- Huawei 950DT based SuperPoD has 8K plus NPUs in scale up domain. 
- If you strictly define scale up as domain over which direct memory Load-Store is is possible, even then the scale up domain has 1024 NPUs.
- WideEP approach allows deploying humongous models on these super pod.
- NPUs have near uniform 3 micro second latency to one another and they can talk any-any with uniform bandwidth. They use optical connectivity, presumably NPO.
- Their HiBL and HiZQ memories have 1.6TB/s and 4TB/s bandwidth. And even with that they can serve large models at high interactivity.

You can read more about this in this article.

quoted_text:
The Clarity Act is dead.

Before the post-mortems and the planning sessions begin, a note of thanks.

Many of you worked extremely hard on this bill over the last 18 months. You fought harder than most people will ever know to make sure we had a good product that actually worked for crypto. It required countless hours of research and analysis; endless calls and meetings to build consensus; rewriting the same sections over and over to find common ground; winning points and making concessions one by one in pursuit of an ambitious goal.

Those efforts were a success. The bill did not pass, but neither did you compromise on your principles or the ultimate goal. It would have been easy to strike deal at any point by simply giving up and rolling over, and you were asked to do so every single day for 18 months. You did not. Your strength, courage, and confidence won the day. You should be proud.

Many of us said since the start of this process that no bill is better than a bad bill, and by that metric, today is a victory. The Senate considered a good bill today, not a perfect one but a good one, and turned it down. The raw politics of the United States during an election year meant a good deal was not on the table. That's okay.

Crypto will be fine without the Clarity Act. We are lucky to have two agencies, the SEC and CFTC, with all of the excellent staff and authority they need to do the job. They're ready to be unleashed, and so they shall be. The future of crypto policy is bright.

Thank you all for your hard work. Breathe a sigh of relief, take a break, and get ready for what's next. We've only just gotten started.

his table tonight?
$2,400

every friday

pause

this dude is making ~$8k/month
and spending over $9k a month
on bottles alone

to impress people
he'll never see again

asked him about the bad months
"what happens when volume dies for a few weeks?"
"volume never dies bro, there's always a runner"

one month later

same guy
posting at 4am
"anyone got a legit caller group? need a W"

wallet down to $600
rent late
friends not answering

now he's aping into every launch
50% of his stack per play
because he can't afford to wait

meanwhile

i spend my fridays at home
cook my own food
rent a normal apartment
split with nobody's expectations

last month:

$55k net from memecoins
kept $30k parked in stables
withdrew $25k to myself
paid myself first
capital second
lifestyle last

the difference:
bottle service guy:
- $8k/month
- $9k+ on weekends
- $0 buffer
- forced to ape when desperate
- one dry month from broke
- flexing on stories
- panicking in DMs

you're rich when a slow month
doesn't change your plans
bottle guy needed an audience
i need a runway
he's one quiet market from done
i'm one good cycle from never needing a job again

but i won't book the table

because i'm not trying to look successful
i'm trying to stay successful
there's a difference between
LOOKING rich on crypto twitter
and ACTUALLY being rich
looking rich:
- bottle pics
- rented lifestyle
- loud stories
- no stables
- no rules
- one dry month = desperation

being rich:
- low expenses
- quiet weekends
- patient entries
- dry powder ready
- slow months absorbed
- never forced to trade
the real whales
don't need the table
they sit in the corner
drink water
and buy when everyone else is scared

the loud ones?
they make $5k to $10k/month
spend it by sunday
and call it "living"
then the market goes quiet
i see it every cycle

a guy hits his first runner
first thought isn't protecting it
it's showing it

club
bottles
trips
rented cars
then volume dries up
and reality shows up
now they're stuck with:
- debts
- no capital
- desperate trades
- no buffer
all because they wanted to LOOK successful
instead of STAYING in the game

that rooftop guy?
six months from now
he'll say
"memecoins are dead"
meanwhile
i'll still be trading
still withdrawing
still home on fridays

the question is simple
do you want the table for a few weekends
and restart every time

or build quietly
and never have to restart again
most will choose the bottles
the few who choose the stables

are the ones who actually make it

text:
this clip is worth watching. ignore how awkward dario is and just listen to the analogy -- especially next to how jensen frames the same thing.

dario compares the AI industry to car companies (maybe a shot at jensen, who knows). he frames the openai incident as "someone's brakes failed and something bad happened," and says the right response isn't to attack the other guy -- it's for the whole industry to think about brake problems, form committees, define standards.

jensen has made a nearly identical analogy, except he states the brake problem as an engineering problem.

so compare them. your brakes are failing. do you fix the brakes so the car actually stops when you need it to, or do you form a committee to discuss how stopping works? pretty clear which one makes sense. fix the damn brakes.

what dario is dancing around -- and what elon has said out loud, repeatedly on twitter -- is that p(doom) doesn't come from the brakes being bad. it comes from the car being smarter than you. and you become the car.

that analogy barely makes sense, but it's more accurate. the actual problem is you can't control something smarter than you. that's a brake problem in the deepest sense, and he didn't touch it here.

which makes me wonder if he ever will, in public, in front of these CEOs. it's a much more direct case for the risk he's actually worried about than "oops my brakes didn't work."

复盘美国参议院近日围绕 CLARITY 法案的表决结果，其最终未能通关其实在意料之中。表面上看是加密行业推进多年的一次立法尝试受挫，但背后折射出的是几方利益在国会博弈中的激烈拉扯：

首先最核心的阻碍依然是伦理争议与党派对立。以参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦为首的民主党人，将矛头直指总统家族在加密领域的巨额商业利益与潜在持仓，对法案中涉及的利益冲突问题提出了严厉批评。

民主党认为，相关条款缺乏对执政高层加密资产的严格硬约束，甚至留有漏洞变相服务于私人产业。在中期选举临近的节点下，两党在这一敏感议题上互不妥协，最终导致共识破裂。

其次是来自传统金融体系的现实压力。传统商业银行与社区银行对合规稳定币可能带来的存款分流保持高度警惕，担忧其对底层信贷产生冲击，因此在国会进行了密集的游说。这种跨行业的利益博弈，让本就脆弱的立法进程更加举步维艰。

最后则是立法日程的紧迫与门槛限制。虽然共和党在投票前夕尝试通过修改部分文本来争取支持，但面对 60 票的参议院通过门槛，最终依然呈现出明显的党派划线，未能达到要求。

不过，法案的搁浅并不意味着行业将进入监管真空。正如多家头部机构在复盘时指出的，后续的监管重心大概率仍会回到 SEC 和 CFTC 的日常行政规则制定中，通过既有框架逐步推进。

短期来看，市场情绪确实需要时间来消化这一政治事件带来的扰动。但从更长远的周期视角来看，政策落地节奏的放缓，也让市场有更多空间去回归宏观基本面的逻辑。

text:
This isn’t the first attempt and won’t be the last.

I worked on silicon-level security to solve for these types of solutions from 2016. We deemed it unviable because it ultimately boiled down to DRM-like capabilities. An actor who found the right vulnerability could violate the contract while appearing compliant, potentially pledging the same compute across multiple exchanges without detection. It was originally part of a range of use cases in confidential computing that a group of us came up with back then.

The harder problem isn’t creating a market for future compute. It’s proving, continuously and across independent markets, that the underlying capacity exists, remains unencumbered, and hasn’t been pledged elsewhere.

We’re already seeing adjacent forms of this problem. A lot of money is being made through nefarious routing arbitrage of models over APIs, en-masse distillation, and secondary markets for call-and-response transcripts.

Do the people that financed this know this already? If so, what could possibly be their justification for this financing decision? It’s not just a problem you can decide to defer to a later round; there’s silicon design needed across all computing.
author: liamjcoff
quoted_text:
How do you assure that the underlying capacity exists and is uniquely available to satisfy an obligation?

There were plenty of attempts at GPU compute futures and future-financing structures during the run-up to and peak of Ethereum mining. The fundamental problem was proving uniqueness of the underlying capacity. Proof of work at least provided observable evidence that the hardware existed and was doing work, but that still didn’t establish that the same future capacity hadn’t been sold or pledged elsewhere.

Many of these structures fell apart even before the market declined. As uncertainty increased, particularly around regulation and the ability to liquidate the underlying assets or contracts, financing became increasingly difficult.

A cash-settled hedge can establish a future price. It does not establish that the underlying compute exists, is unencumbered, or is uniquely available to satisfy the obligation.

I have serious doubts about this. It looks like some of the same structural problems are being rediscovered with fresh eyes and fresh money.

text:
General Mohan Singh Founder and 1st Commander-in-Chief INA
As unveiled in the Indian Heritage Centre (IHC) Singapore today.

The INA is most famously associated with Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, but it was in fact founded by a young Captain in the 1/14 Punjab Regiment, Mohan Singh. Unknown outside his unit, he was chosen by the Japanese in Dec 1941 to start & command the INA, that, they said, would be armed and supported to invade India and free it of British rule. He grew into the role and wore the mantle effectively, at times harshly, resulting in 90% of the Indian POWs in Singapore volunteering.

Singh was no pushover and knew what the Japanese were capable of. Of this alliance with them he said “Whether I believed the Japanese to be sincere at that time it was very difficult for me to decide. Even if chances of sincerity were 1 to 10, I wanted to test it. It was worth it. In any way it was going to bring out the truth. If they were trying to use us as it suited them, we were also trying to use them as it suited us. I was prepared for both eventualities”. (source his post-war interrogation)

He soon realized Japanese promises were hollow, and at great risk to his life, refused to cooperate and was arrested and exiled on 29Dec1942. On his orders, the INA was disbanded.

It was then that the Japanese asked Hitler to send Bose to Asia (he had been in Berlin since 1941) and it was after his arrival in Singapore in July 1943 that the more well-known narrative begins. Indeed, Netaji took the movement to greater heights, but without General Mohan Singh and other stalwarts Giani Pritam Singh and Rash Bahari Bose who built the alliance with Japan before the war, Bose would not have been called to Asia and go on to fulfill his tryst with destiny.

We must thank IHC Singapore that they have recognized the role of General Mohan Singh, an unsung hero of India.

The images are of General Mohan Singh/ Netaji and the description below (items 4/5). The General’s image is taken from his interrogation report, the longest at over 200 pages of an INA soldier/ civilian in the movement. His interrogator Maj Hugh Toye could not help hiding his admiration while describing him, and at great risk to his own reputation amongst fellow Britons, included in it this defiant image of Singh speaking in Bangkok June 1942. Several copies were made and Toye kept one for himself. Decades later they were reacquainted and he handed it over to Singh’s son as a personal tribute. This image is reproduced from that special document, now in the family archives and it is indeed a privilege to play a part in making this happen.

text:
Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: https://t.co/eoLGVY8yad

Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

The reality is:

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

- Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well.

Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us. I'm proud of the security foundations we've built.

- Engaging independent evaluators and advisors is industry best practice. MSL already does this today in several areas because it helps produce better work. Other labs can just do this too. In general, it would be helpful for there to be a larger and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators.

- Committing the significant majority of compute towards serving people rather than racing towards recursive self-improvement is one of the best ways to ensure we develop this technology safely. Meta has made this commitment and other labs can do this as well.

I believe the key to building a positive future for everyone is maintaining the right balance of power. This is within our power to do.

text:
[ 저커버그 "속도 늦추자는 요구 없이 우리는 이미 안전하게 만들고 있다" ]

마크 저커버그가 아모데이의 "We Must Pace the Frontier" 에세이가 나온 지 며칠 만에 공개 반박에 나섰다. 

업계 전체가 속도를 늦추자고 호소할 필요 없이, 각 연구소가 자기 모델을 안전하게 학습시킬 책임과 유인, 그리고 실행 능력을 이미 갖고 있다는 게 핵심 논리다.

메타는 Muse 출시를 안전과 보안 점검 때문에 몇 달 미뤘는데.. 남들에게 먼저 하라고 요구하지 않고 그냥 일상 업무로 처리했다는 얘기를 근거로 든다.

논리 구조는 네 가지. 

사람들은 자기 뜻대로 움직이지 않는 에이전트를 쓰지 않으니 정렬 자체가 경쟁력이 되고, 정렬에 소홀한 연구소는 뒤처진다. 

모델이 해를 끼치면 연구소가 막대한 법적 책임을 지니 사고를 막을 유인이 이미 있다. 

독립 평가자 참여는 업계 관행이라 누구나 하면 된다. 

그리고 컴퓨팅의 대부분을 재귀적 자기개선 경쟁이 아니라 사람에게 서비스하는 데 쓰겠다는 약속을 메타가 먼저 했으니 다른 곳도 따라오면 된다.

바탕에는 8월에 낸 장문의 선언문 "The Future is for Everyone"이 있다. 

자비로운 단일 초지능이란 존재하지 않으며, 안전은 기술적 정렬이 아니라 힘의 균형에서 나오고, 이 균형은 초지능을 개인에게 널리 나눠줄 때 개인 쪽으로 기운다는 주장이다. 

해당 틀에서 보면 정렬을 이유로 진도를 늦추거나 강력한 모델을 연구소가 붙들고 있는 것은 가장 위험한 시나리오이며 중앙집중으로 가는 길이 된다. 

다른 연구소들은 기업과 정부를 위한 AI를 만들고 있어 그들이 앞서면 힘이 기관 쪽으로 쏠린다는 비판도 담겨 있다.

안전을 놓고 두 개의 정의가 정면으로 맞붙었다. 

아모데이는 안전이 통제와 속도 조절에서 나온다고 보고, 저커버그는 안전이 분산과 경쟁에서 나온다고 보고있다.

text:
: : [Institution/Report] Beyond the Dollar: The Conditions for Sovereign Debt Tokenization, and Why Korea Is the First Clean Test
Written by Sam Shim (Meritz Securities), Data supported by @100y_eth 

- Tokenized US Treasuries reached about 15.9 billion dollars in July 2026, and technology was only part of it. The dollar market had supplied a fund structure institutions were allowed to hold, demand that existed before the first token, and recurring fee income.

- Token standards, custody, and settlement are now available off the shelf, so infrastructure is no longer the constraint. Products outside the dollar are still under a tenth of tokenized government debt, and that number measures what has been built rather than what investors want.

- Demand starts with stablecoin reserves, because a coin wants its backing in its own currency and onchain. Only a tokenized government bond in that currency is both, which makes reserves the only demand proven so far, while collateral and diversification have not appeared yet.

- Korea has most of what that demand sequence needs in one market, and foreign investors can already buy its bonds. Bond sourcing and won conversion run through domestic infrastructure, and a won stablecoin already holds a tokenized Korean government bond in reserve, though only at symbolic size.

- The whole argument rests on one bet, that what is missing is the product, not the appetite. The strongest objection is that onchain capital structurally prefers the dollar, and the report sets out the evidence that would settle it stage by stage.

Full Report:
https://t.co/22IZiY0rgN

text:
Researchers argue LLMs don't actually understand anything.

They call it "Potemkin Understanding."

For years, we’ve evaluated AI using human tests. The Bar Exam. AP Tests. The MMLU.

When a model aces these tests, we assume it understands the concepts. Because if a human passes the test, they fundamentally understand the material.

But that assumption is fatally flawed.

Humans make predictable mistakes. When we misunderstand something, there is a logical pattern to our errors.

The researchers discovered that AI does not fail like a human.

It fails like an illusion.

They ran an experiment. They asked top models to define complex concepts from game theory, literature, and psychology.

The AI nailed the definitions perfectly.

Then, they asked the AI to do something simple: identify a real-world example of the exact concept it just defined.

Performance completely collapsed.

Even worse, when researchers asked the AI to generate a custom example, the AI later failed to correctly classify its own generated output.

The models were fundamentally incoherent.

They exhibited up to a 62% failure rate the moment they had to actually apply the knowledge they just flawlessly defined.

The models aren’t reasoning. They are just reciting memorized patterns wrapped in a conversational tone.

The researchers named it after a Potemkin village, a fake, hollow facade designed to look impressive from the outside, with absolutely nothing behind it.

Every major AI company is selling you intelligence based on benchmark scores.

But this paper proves those benchmarks are a mirage.

text:
Woz is back!

 I am his first customer. 

He got my career started.

I stuffed so many of his motherboards as a kid.

While we sat around and watched TV.

My dad built custom holders so we could stuff them while sitting on the couch. And a custom set of wires to take away any static electricity.

I once got to interview Woz in front of UC Berkeley’s business school. Said they had fewer failures than the ones built in its own factory.

What we didn’t discuss is how much love we put into them.

They were technology from an alien world.

There wasn’t anything else like it in my life.

Woz is still the nicest founder I have ever met. 

And the original nerd. 

As I get older I realize how special those few hundred hours spent with him were. Not to mention he gave me $40,000 worth of Mac’s to run the school paper on. And I remember thinking to myself, as we sat in the cafeteria of West Valley Community College, “can’t get that kind of education at Stanford.”

When @elonmusk talks about putting love into his products, I get that deeply.

text:
如果你看ETF数据，今天净流入，明天净流出，后天又净流入，大后天又净流出，这能说明什么？是不是感觉很懵逼？

但其实不用那么复杂。要了解到底是卖的多，还是买的多，看余额不就好了吗？余额的趋势变化更能反映整体参与者的心态和行为。

当前美国BTC现货ETF的总余额是126.5w枚BTC；其中贝莱德的IBIT和富达的FBTC合计占了76%，所以我们就看这两家，其他可以不用看。

而且，在通常意义上贝莱德机构占比更多，富达本身也是美国最大的零售券商之一。分别对比2家的数据，就更有意思了：

IBIT的余额峰值出现在今年5月，而不是牛市顶部。看样子贝莱德的客户们从2月就开始抄底了，到5月持仓已高达82.2w枚BTC，创历史新高。

7月最低为72.9w枚，此后又开始一路上扬。到9月3日共增加5.5w枚。关键是从9/3-9/4这段，BTC价格下跌，但余额并未减少，对短期价格波动不敏感。

而FBTC就和IBIT完全不同。它的余额峰值就出现在牛市的顶点，此后价格一路下跌，余额也持续减少。在今年2-5月期间只是大体维持，完全没有增持的迹象。

8月16日FBTC的余额降至最低，只有17w枚BTC。也就是说，本轮拉升之前FBTC的客户们还在不停的卖。这是典型的“散户行为”，和当时推特上看4w/3w的悲观情绪完全吻合。

此后，随着价格拉升，FBTC的余额增加了5-6k枚。不算多，但从9/3-9/4这段来看，同样也没有明显减少。

所以，综合来看，至少目前美国投资者的情绪还算稳定，没有因为宏观的不确定性而重回恐慌。

但2家主要购买力显然还都未开启暴走模式，余额离前高也还有一定差距。所以，现阶段最多只能算熊牛过渡期，牛回应该还早。
author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
ETF的净流量数据是怎么来的？其中的BTC上链吗？

看到评论区有小伙伴对ETF的流程有疑问，前几天也有小伙伴聊到ETF的BTC上不上链，正好一起将这2个问题讲清楚。

我们举例说明👉

假设：IBIT信托持有60w枚BTC（$63,000），已发行份额66亿份，那么NAV = 600,000 × 63,000 ÷ 6,600,000,000 ≈ $5.73。代表每一份IBIT对应大概0.0000909枚BTC，值$5.73。

假设某天交易所里卖单太多，买盘接不住，虽然NAV是$5.73，但市价被砸到了$5.67，出现约1%的贴水。

这时，对AP来说就是一个无风险的套利机会。同一个东西，二级市场卖$5.67，但它背后的BTC却值$5.73。

于是AP会这么做：

1⃣ 在交易所花567w美元买入100万份IBIT；
2⃣ 把这100万份交给贝莱德，并按NAV赎回。
3⃣ 信托注销份额，并把对应的90.9枚BTC从信托资产中划出。
（现金模式下，信托把这些BTC卖掉，将现金付给AP；实物模式下，直接把90.9枚BTC给AP）

成本$567w，到手$573w，扣掉成本剩下的就是净利润。同时，AP在二级市场买ETF，会让市价向NAV收敛，当套利窗口关闭，AP就停手了。

整个过程中真正的资产变化，是信托的BTC少了90.9枚，已发行份额少了100万份。而“净流量”数据统计的就是这个，当日份额的净增减，再折成BTC或美元。

反过来也一样：当市场买盘汹涌产生了溢价，那AP就在二级市场卖出ETF份额，同时向发行方按NAV申购新份额，信托拿到钱就去买BTC；份额增加，记为净流入。

追溯“净流入/净流出”的源头，其实就是二级市场那笔没人接的买压/卖压。

我们在关注净流量的同时，也要结合成交量一起看。“高成交+高流出”和“低成交+高流出”，背后的信息是不一样的。

另外，当日的净赎回/申购，都要会在托管专户的冷钱包和Coinbase的交易账户之间调用或归集。托管账户的进出，本质上是净流量数据的链上镜像。

所以，ETF净流量数据全部上链，只有二级份额转让才不上链。

text:
少见的马斯克居然公开点赞扎克伯格了。

正常来说，当前很多人对 AI 威胁论的看法，是模型越强，就应该越限制它，只开放给少数人和机构使用。

但 Meta 的扎克伯格认为，前沿的 AI 模型，不应该被少数人使用，而是开放给全人类。

因为危险主要来自权力集中。例如少数实验室、政府或机构掌握超级智能，比模型本身更危险。

所以更安全的路径，是把超级智能，广泛分发给几十亿人，都可以使用，这样彼此之间能形成相互制衡。

目前 OpenAI、Anthropic、谷歌，都倾向于给前沿 AI 设发展限制，他们担心能力跑得太快，人类来不及理解和控制，容易被滥用。

预计未来大家会就此观点，形成两派人群，估计要争论不休了。

quoted_text:
Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: https://t.co/eoLGVY8yad

Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

The reality is:

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

- Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well.

Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us. I'm proud of the security foundations we've built.

- Engaging independent evaluators and advisors is industry best practice. MSL already does this today in several areas because it helps produce better work. Other labs can just do this too. In general, it would be helpful for there to be a larger and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators.

- Committing the significant majority of compute towards serving people rather than racing towards recursive self-improvement is one of the best ways to ensure we develop this technology safely. Meta has made this commitment and other labs can do this as well.

I believe the key to building a positive future for everyone is maintaining the right balance of power. This is within our power to do.

: : [Crypto/Report] All About x402
Written by @Jun__Yoo 

As agents begin to make purchasing decisions and execute purchases, the way APIs, data, and computing resources are traded will change. x402 is an open payment specification that integrates pricing, payment authorization, and settlement into software workflows. What markets will emerge, and who will capture the economic value?

All About x402 explores the protocol’s core architecture and extensions, then examines how agentic commerce could evolve. It analyzes market scenarios based on the scope of delegated purchasing authority, examines value capture across ecosystem participants, and compares how Cloudflare, AWS, Google, and Fastly are integrating agent payments into their existing businesses.

The report also brings together perspectives from ecosystem participants building and using x402. From the value of precise data to service quality, trust, and payment rail neutrality, it addresses the questions that must be resolved for agent payments to develop into a functioning market.

Tomorrow, one possible outcome after the Fed hiked, is that we may discover that tightening doesn’t lower long-term yields. If that happens, it would confirm that fiscal is the culprit in the whodunnit saga.

By raising the government’s marginal funding cost, a rate hike enlarges future interest deficits and increases the amount of debt Treasury must place with private investors. If investors doubt that fiscal policy will offset those costs, the term premium could rise, pushing long yields higher and reinforcing the deterioration in debt service.

text:
I run message discipline for the Pentagon's public affairs shop. My job is making sure the Secretary, the Chief of Naval Operations, and every combatant commander say the same sentence when a reporter asks the same question. This week, none of them did.

Sunday, Adm. Brad Cooper told CBS he's "not concerned at all" about munitions. Monday, the Pentagon's own Inspector General released its report. Not a leak. Not a think tank. The building auditing itself. $22.3 billion in munitions expended since February. $33.4 billion in total war costs. The report doesn't use the word "shortfall." It says the Pentagon is working "to stockpile critical materials, components, and selected munitions to respond rapidly to a contingency." I know the difference between those two phrases better than any reporter does. Picking the word is the job.

One day. That's the gap between the confidence and the audit. I didn't have to find a contradiction. The building filed its own.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao is not supposed to describe damage assessments in those terms. He described the February strike on our Bahrain base by saying it "blew the hell out of Bahrain." That's a real sentence. Said by a real Secretary. Into a real microphone. I have a slide about microphone discipline. I built it myself.

The Chief of Naval Operations went further. At a recent town hall, asked about getting the Bahrain facility back online, he said we're not getting back in there anytime soon. Then he added that he wanted to be completely honest about that. Honesty was the part he flagged as unusual. He wasn't wrong to flag it.

A Wall Street Journal estimate puts the Bahrain rebuild at more than 400 million dollars, and an official said that could be low. That's the number I keep out of the next briefing. Not because it's classified. Because it's inconvenient, and inconvenient doesn't need a classification to disappear from a slide.

The President posted that we have virtually unlimited amounts of ammunition. He also said this war would end in early April. Both statements are still on his own feed. Neither one required my approval. I only handle the sentences that go out under someone else's name.

I've had three principals go off the same script in one week, and an Inspector General file the fourth contradiction from inside the building. My review this quarter says crisis communications leadership. Nobody's asked me to be more careful about the truth. They've asked me to be faster about the sentence that replaces it.

I already have next week's version drafted. It says we remain confident in our posture. It's shorter than this one. Shorter tests better.

text:
I don't understand how anyone can be lazy in 2026.

The ENTIRE internet is literally up for grabs.

SaaS, agencies, content businesses - we're living in a gold rush moment with AI.

If I wanted to start my first $10k/mo AI side hustle, this is exactly what I'd do (no BS):

Step One: Finding overlap with your existing skills

If you want to print cash, you need to find a business model that overlaps with what you already know.

Stop asking AI for a list of business ideas.

My advice: ask AI to interview you and extract ideas based on your existing skill set (GPT-6 Astra is scary good at this).

You'll always make more money on something you know manually and can then amplify with AI.

Step Two: Pick one of two bizz models

For beginners, there are two businesses you should consider:

1. Consulting: Solve ONE painful problem (leads, follow-ups, admin) with AI and charge to implement a solution.

2. Digital products: Sell the same digital thing repeatedly. More scalable. Tools, templates, agents, courses. The hard part here is distribution.

Consulting = speed, digital products = scale.

3. Validating PFM

This is the step everyone skips, and it's the most important.

AI can spin up a great-sounding idea in seconds, but the market decides if it's worth paying for.

Before building anything, you should talk to real business owners with the problem you're aiming to solve.

Ask what they would want, ideal outcomes, etc.

4. Build the launch kit w/ AI

Once you've validated an idea, you can build the entire launch kit with AI.

• Landing page
• Pricing
• Offer
• Copy
• CRM/customer database

5. Landing your first customer

Your first goal isn't money; it's proof.

Complete one real implementation, then capture it: what was the problem, what you built, what changed, would they recommend it. That's your first case study.

Then document it publicly:

→ "I helped a local business automate its follow-ups"
→ "I built my first paid AI tool from scratch"
→ "Documenting my journey from $0 to $10k/mo"

Real work → proof → authority → inbound leads.

TL;DR: the whole playbook is: finding a problem, validating it, building a useful offer, getting proof, repeating what works.

I have a hot take about Clarity that I'm surprised I'm not seeing on the timeline. 

In the last election, the industry was left with two very bad choices. The Dems were politicizing all things crypto at the behest of Warren/Gensler and unfairly targeting them for god knows what reason -- a political power play? Being paid by China to ensure the US is no longer at the frontier of tech and finance? Only God knows.

In comes Trump, promising to be The Crypto President, promising the crypto community that if they vote for him, he will get rid of Gensler, create a bitcoin stockpile, protect self-custody, etc. 

But come on, how many people didn't know, based on his track record, that this would be a deal with the devil? And if they didn't know it then, then how many people still didn't know it after he launched a memecoin during the Crypto Ball and became the Max Extractor in Chief? (Also, let's not forget about solana:FUAfBo2jgks6gB4Z4LfZkqSZgzNucisEHqnNebaRxM1P.) The fact is that if the President and his family hadn't done so much crypto self-dealing during this administration, then Clarity would have had much better odds of passing. In fact, I would dare say it likely would have passed. 

The last time Kristin Smith was on my show, she said at this point, all the details about crypto had been worked out, and the main issues left to negotiate had to do with ethics. Basically, the remaining issues had to do with the president, and not crypto or Clarity itself. 

So, did the crypto industry shoot itself in the foot by throwing its lot in with Trump? I'm not saying that Kamala would have for sure been the better choice, but I do think it's worth asking this question.

quoted_text:
Now the #1 holder on @fomo for $kled, so I wanted to share my thesis publicly before what I think could be one of the crazier runs in Solana onchain history begins.

We’ve watched Solana onchain and onchain in general evolve in real time.

We went from a few memes absorbing most of the liquidity, to the proliferation of memes, to launchpads, to tokens offering reflections, and even the AI-meme / quasi tech product narrative that dominated parts of the last cycle.

But I think the next, and potentially final evolution of onchain is much bigger than memes.

It’s access to a new and fairer frontier for venture capital markets.

What has kept me so bullish for onchain this long is my thesis on what these markets could become at maturity: the easiest, most accessible form of non-exclusive venture capital in the world.

For too long, private investors and VC firms have been given access to extremely lucrative private rounds while the general public gets access only after a company is mature enough to IPO, often when early investors are looking for exit liquidity.

That system excludes the vast majority of people and dumps on them in the process. 

There needs to be a way for a savvy investor or founder, regardless of their wealth or connections, to get exposure to promising young companies and capital while they are still a young org.

That’s why I’m so proud of what @avipat_  and the @useKled team have built and shared so far. 

https://t.co/whx42lj5Es has surpassed 500,000 users likely much more by now, with hundreds of millions of files uploaded, and is essentially building the Uber of private data collection. You have valuable data or content? Now you can earn off it as opposed to big tech scraping it without your permission. 

And here’s the part I find especially interesting:

Through @StreetFDN’s novel SPV structure, $kled token holders have exposure to 5–10% of the equity in the company, subject to the applicable structure and terms.

The company has raised at a multi-nine-figure valuation, and the team has been heads-down for months building V3, a product evolution where $kled and its flywheel become an integral part of their broader ecosystem.

There’s no one I’d rather bet on in Solana onchain than Avi and his team because they have shown at every turn a desire to lead the revolution of internet capital markets. 

I’ve watched him repeatedly try to push the space forward, often taking risks with a company that could be successful without ever having a token.

He doesn’t have to give the public a seat at the table.

But he is.

He’s giving people a chance to participate in the growth curve of a company at a valuation they otherwise would never have had access to.

So, tip of the hat to him and his team. 

Companies that follow in his footseps will also become heroes in the onchain community.  Finding capital and loyal users.  This is the final evolution of solona onchain imo. Token tied to equity. Let the freemarket decide your value in real time. 

I’m currently the largest $kled holder on FOMO, because the team is cooking. 

My speculation is that V3 could arrive alongside renewed attention around the Anthropic and OpenAI IPO stories. If AI becomes the dominant narrative again, I think Kled has a uniquely positioned story:

Own your data.

And if you want to monetize it, you should have the ability to do so through a trusted intermediary, rather than having your data extracted and monetized by AI labs without meaningful participation.

That is the bigger thesis for me.

Not just another meme.

Not just another token.

A market for data ownership, participation, and access to private-company upside, built onchain.

Kled is currently valued @ $14m market cap. It has been sitting in roughly this range for months, but it’s beginning to slowly creep higher.

I think people are starting to anticipate the move.

And if Avi gets loud again on socials while V3 is ready to ship, I think Kled is going to get very interesting.

text:
UGANDA MUST STOP ATTRACTING INVESTORS WITH ONE HAND AND FRUSTRATE THEM WITH THE OTHER:

Special appreciation to UIA for its efforts to attract investment into Uganda. The numbers show that UIA is doing important work: in FY2024/25, UIA licensed 481 investment projects, with a projected investment value of US$3.2 billion and an expected 53,230 direct jobs. FDI inflows also rose from US$2.99 billion to US$3.5 billion. 

HOWEVER here is the uncomfortable question: What happens after UIA brings the investor to Uganda?

This is where Uganda's investment strategy needs a serious Government-wide rethink.

1. TAXATION
URA must be a revenue collector without becoming an agency that inadvertently destroys the tax base.
A young business that has barely established itself needs predictable, proportionate and professional tax administration—not tax assessments capable of pushing it into insolvency.

The concerns surrounding disputed tax assessments are real. By June 2025, 500 tax cases worth about Shs1.5 trillion remained unresolved before the Tax Appeals Tribunal.

Gov't  should be asking: “How do we collect the right tax while keeping the business alive?”

2. INVESTMENT CAPITAL MUST MOVE WITH PREDICTABILITY
Foreign investors must have confidence that legitimate capital can enter Uganda through a transparent, predictable and timely regulatory process.
Any complaints of excessive delays, unexplained requirements or misconduct in financial-clearance processes should be independently investigated and resolved.

3. THE MULTIPLE-LICENSING PROBLEM

E.g why should an investor establishing a manufacturing plant have to navigate multiple institutions dealing separately with environmental approvals, local government licences, building approvals, standards certification, immigration and taxation?
Uganda already recognised this problem when UIA established its One Stop Centre, bringing together 12 Government departments involved in investment facilitation.
We should now go further.
One investor. One digital file. One coordinated Government process. One accountable officer.

4. DIGITISATION MUST MEAN SPEED
Putting bureaucracy online does not eliminate bureaucracy.
The Government's eBiz platform already integrates services including company registration, investment licensing and tax identification.
But the real test is not whether an application can be submitted online.
The real test is: HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO GET THE APPROVAL?
An investor cannot be told that Uganda is open for business and then wait weeks or months for routine approvals.

5. CORRUPTION IS AN INVISIBLE INVESTMENT TAX
President Museveni himself has identified corruption by officials demanding bribes for land and licences as a major impediment to lowering the cost of doing business.
This must be confronted head-on.
If an investor discovers that paying a bribe is the fastest way to obtain a Government service, then we have created an unofficial tax on investment.
And unlike a statutory tax, corruption produces no public infrastructure, no jobs and no development.

6. COMMERCIAL JUSTICE MUST MOVE AT THE SPEED OF BUSINESS
An investor can survive a difficult negotiation. An investor can survive paying legitimate taxes.
An investor cannot easily survive having billions of shillings trapped in litigation for years.

Uganda has previously reported trillions of shillings locked in unresolved commercial disputes. Earlier estimates put the figure at Shs8 trillion, while more recent reporting continues to show substantial capital trapped in Commercial Court disputes.
Capital trapped in litigation is capital not creating jobs, paying suppliers, producing goods or generating taxes.

THE POLITICAL QUESTION
Government should therefore establish a Presidential/Prime Ministerial Investment Facilitation Task Force bringing together UIA, URA, NEMA, URSB, UNBS, KCCA, Immigration, FIA and the Judiciary to identify and eliminate the institutional bottlenecks frustrating investors.

text:
It’s weird tech on the surface. I watched the video and wasn’t sure how Jev fit into my workflow. 

It doesn’t write, plan, or run the loop, so next to Claude/GPT it looked kind of pointless.

However, after thinking for a bit, what it actually is: a cheap judgment call you can put around the models you already use. And that’s pretty useful. 

Examples that made more sense to me:

•  don’t send every request to an LLM. Have it decide “is this even a generation task?” first

•  agent with 80 tools / 200 files - rank the options instead of dumping the whole list into context. My agents are often retarded at tool calls. 

•  after a model drafts a patch or reply, ask “does this actually address the ticket?” / “is this tool call sketchy?” before you execute it

The LLM still does the writing and reasoning. Your code still owns the workflow. 

This just answers the fuzzy questions so the program can branch without spending a frontier call on every little decision.

It’s not trying to replace your current models. More like something you can afford to run on every step, not just the final answer.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ pretty cool actually!

text:
I recently supported Meritz Securities, one of Korea’s major securities firms, on a report exploring the tokenization of Korean government bonds 🇰🇷

This comes at a pretty interesting time. Korea’s FSC recently announced plans to expand tokenization beyond fractional/alternative assets to conventional securities like stocks, bonds, and funds.

And imo that part matters a lot. 

If tokenization is going to grow into a market of meaningful scale, bringing traditional securities onchain will be key and government bonds are arguably the biggest opportunity.

Today, though, the onchain government bond market is still overwhelmingly centered around U.S. Treasuries.

So where would demand for tokenized Korean government bonds actually come from? And what needs to happen for KTBs to successfully move onchain?

👇
author: 100y_eth
quoted_text:
: : [Institution/Report] Beyond the Dollar: The Conditions for Sovereign Debt Tokenization, and Why Korea Is the First Clean Test
Written by Sam Shim (Meritz Securities), Data supported by @100y_eth 

- Tokenized US Treasuries reached about 15.9 billion dollars in July 2026, and technology was only part of it. The dollar market had supplied a fund structure institutions were allowed to hold, demand that existed before the first token, and recurring fee income.

- Token standards, custody, and settlement are now available off the shelf, so infrastructure is no longer the constraint. Products outside the dollar are still under a tenth of tokenized government debt, and that number measures what has been built rather than what investors want.

- Demand starts with stablecoin reserves, because a coin wants its backing in its own currency and onchain. Only a tokenized government bond in that currency is both, which makes reserves the only demand proven so far, while collateral and diversification have not appeared yet.

- Korea has most of what that demand sequence needs in one market, and foreign investors can already buy its bonds. Bond sourcing and won conversion run through domestic infrastructure, and a won stablecoin already holds a tokenized Korean government bond in reserve, though only at symbolic size.

- The whole argument rests on one bet, that what is missing is the product, not the appetite. The strongest objection is that onchain capital structurally prefers the dollar, and the report sets out the evidence that would settle it stage by stage.

Full Report:

text:
this clip is worth watching. ignore how awkward dario is and just listen to the analogy -- especially next to how jensen frames the same thing.

dario compares the AI industry to car companies (maybe a shot at jensen, who knows). he frames the openai incident as "someone's brakes failed and something bad happened," and says the right response isn't to attack the other guy -- it's for the whole industry to think about brake problems, form committees, define standards.

jensen has made a nearly identical analogy, except he states the brake problem as an engineering problem.

so compare them. your brakes are failing. do you fix the brakes so the car actually stops when you need it to, or do you form a committee to discuss how stopping works? pretty clear which one makes sense. fix the damn brakes.

what dario is dancing around -- and what elon has said out loud, repeatedly on twitter -- is that p(doom) doesn't come from the brakes being bad. it comes from the car being smarter than you. and you become the car.

that analogy barely makes sense, but it's more accurate. the actual problem is you can't control something smarter than you. that's a brake problem in the deepest sense, and he didn't touch it here.

which makes me wonder if he ever will, in public, in front of these CEOs. it's a much more direct case for the risk he's actually worried about than "oops my brakes didn't work."

https://t.co/9Qxh4JXaQz, a New York-based payments startup, emerged from stealth Tuesday with a $20 million seed round that closed in August. The round was led by Expa and Uber cofounder Garrett Camp, with participation from Coinbase Ventures, Tenet Fund, the founders of Figure, Mesh founder Bam Azizi, Second Sight Ventures, and sovereign and royal family offices in the Gulf and Africa. Cofounders Nabeel Alamgir and Mustafa Dar declined to disclose the company's valuation.

https://t.co/9Qxh4JXaQz sells white-label payment infrastructure to businesses including financial services firms, consumer platforms and prediction markets. Its tools let prediction market users fund wallets from exchanges such as Binance and https://t.co/6hEdsLgFzg, and help platforms move corporate funds across borders. The company declined to name specific clients but said they collectively serve more than 800 million users. Alamgir frames the mission as a last-mile problem: "We believe that money movement is like a plane taking off from one airport, but it has to land somewhere else." The name https://t.co/9Qxh4JXaQz abbreviates "finishing the job."

The startup enters a crowded field that includes Circle, BVNK and Bridge, the stablecoin infrastructure provider owned by Stripe. Stablecoin market capitalization surpassed $305 billion in September, up more than 77% year over year, according to DeFiLlama, after Congress passed the Genius Act in July 2025 establishing a federal framework for dollar-pegged stablecoins. Alamgir and Dar acknowledged the competition but said their personal experience shapes https://t.co/9Qxh4JXaQz's regional focus on South Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Both grew up watching their parents send money overseas. The company has offices in New York, Las Vegas, Dubai, Dhaka, Bangalore and Lahore.
