text:
One thing I didn't focus on enough in my last post about @TrezuApp is the lack of commercial confidentiality in crypto.

Once someone links a wallet to your company, they can start estimating your budgets, salaries, contractor payments, or even how much runway you have left.

That can give contractors leverage in negotiations and competitors insight into how your business operates.

Essentially, Trezu lets teams hold crypto, pay employees and contractors, swap tokens, and manage payment approvals in one place, with the option to keep your finances private.

Governance stays public and verifiable. Finances stay private.

With Confidential Treasuries, anyone can see the multisig members and that a vote took place, but they can't see how much money the treasury holds or who the team is paying.

The confidential treasury runs on a private shard on @NEARProtocol, letting teams:

→ Keep treasury balances private
→ Keep payment proposals visible only to the team
→ Pay contractors in batches with multisig approvals

And when you pay a contractor’s public wallet, the money arrives from a generic NEAR Intents address. Someone checking that wallet would see a transfer from a smart contract, without a direct public link back to your company’s treasury.

So if you’re managing company funds onchain, you can create a confidential treasury for free: https://t.co/IlP1eO86JE
author: stacy_muur
quoted_text:
As a founder, I’ve been trying to move away from relying on one seed phrase to protect everything I own onchain.

So should YOU.

I came across @TrezuApp, which uses a non-custodial multisig to remove the single point of failure that comes with relying on one wallet or seed phrase.

Here’s a quick TL;DR ↓

1️⃣ Architecture

The treasury is a multisig smart contract on @NEARProtocol.

Trezu uses a multisig setup where each team member connects with their own wallet.

Nobody shares one login, and Trezu doesn’t hold the team’s private keys, so all the funds remain under the treasury’s control onchain.

More importantly, responsibilities are separated by permissions:

→ Requestors can create payment, swap, staking, or withdrawal requests, but can’t approve them.

→ Ops team can approve or reject requests, but can’t edit them or change the treasury setup.

→ Governance controls members, voting thresholds, and request settings, but can’t approve normal payments.

In a nutshell, an employee from the Marketing department can prepare a $100K payment without having the ability to actually move $100K.

Execution still depends on the approval threshold the company configured, for example, a 2-of-3 multisig.

As a founder, you can delegate operations without delegating unilateral control of the money.

2️⃣ Approval Layer

When someone creates a payment request, they have to enter the wallet address, token, amount, and network before it goes to Finance or Ops for review.

The responsible department sees exactly who's getting paid, how much, which token, and any comment the Requestor left with it.

And because the request can't be edited once it's submitted, nobody can change the details after the first person has looked at it.

If there aren't enough tokens in the treasury, the payment can't be approved until the team tops it up. Once it's completed, Trezu generates a PDF receipt as proof of payment.

I know it sounds like boring admin stuff, but crypto payments are irreversible, and having the details tied to the request means more than "trust me bro".

3️⃣ Bulk Payments

For bulk payments, a Requestor can upload a CSV with wallet addresses and amounts, or enter them manually. The whole batch goes through as one request.

One limitation worth knowing is that everyone in the batch needs to be paid in the same token.

So it’s ideal for $USDC contractor payments, but not for one batch where everyone wants a different asset.

Finance then reviews the batch before funds move and can reject it if anything looks off.

I bet you won’t find many founders who enjoy clicking through a million separate wallet prompts lol.

4️⃣ Self-Custody Layer

This is one of the first things I look for with any self-custody product:

→ The funds aren’t sitting in a Trezu-controlled account!

They remain onchain and are controlled by the treasury setup and the team’s signing wallets.

If the Trezu app becomes unavailable, the company can still interact with the treasury through alternative onchain interfaces or command-line tooling.

5️⃣ Multichain Infrastructure

Trezu supports treasury management across networks including @ethereum, @solana, @Bitcoin, @0xPolygon, @NEARProtocol, @SuiNetwork, @ton_blockchain, and @Cardano.

For a company operating across multiple ecosystems, that matters.

Instead of rebuilding completely different operational processes every time the company starts using another network, the team gets one place to manage treasury activity and approvals.

IMO, most teams don’t think seriously about treasury infrastructure until they DO.

Once a company has its one-year runway onchain, one compromised laptop, employee, or seed phrase shouldn’t be enough to drain everything.

That’s the real appeal of multisig that not many people get:

Delegate the work without giving any single person unilateral control of the treasury.

Trezu is free to create and has no asset or user caps. They’ve already processed $194M+ in transactions, manage $100M in assets, and are used by 433 teams.

If you're a founder struggling to manage company funds onchain without relying on one wallet or one person, check out: https://t.co/3EBdZMbRGg

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Is an Architecture Reset, Not Just a Cheaper Model
Despite having more total and active parameters than its predecessor, V4.1 Flash cuts working KV cache to one quarter and persistent cache storage to one eighth.
Zhihu contributor Exhalation explains how it does this by deleting old modules, sharing KV states, and recomputing local context.

1️⃣ DeepSeek removed its own previous ideas
🔹 MTP: external draft models such as DSpark weakened its speculative-decoding value, while the auxiliary loss no longer justified its memory cost.
🔹 Heavily Compressed Attention: its global-summary role was ambiguous and difficult to combine with FP4 storage.
🔹 Dense warmup: V4.1 trains sparse attention from scratch rather than starting with one trillion dense-attention tokens.

2️⃣ Store less, reuse more
Non-SWA KV cache moves from FP8 to FP4, while the more sensitive SWA portion remains FP8.
DeepSeek no longer persists SWA cache. When a conversation forks from an earlier point, the system rebuilds only a small local window. Post-training simulated this process to limit numerical drift.
A modified YOCO design provides the other major saving. Upper layers reuse the same lower-layer source representation, adding only a layer-specific projection.
The result is roughly half the KV storage and close to 50% less historical prefill computation in the idealized case.

3️⃣ Sparse attention reuses its search
Sparse attention lowers attention cost from O(n²) to O(kn), but finding the top-k tokens can still retain an O(n²) component.
V4.1 Flash either reuses an earlier layer’s top-k result or selects a smaller candidate-block pool before re-indexing.
This prevents token selection from becoming the bottleneck at long context lengths.

4️⃣ Engram and mHC were streamlined
Engram replaces an expensive second-order optimizer state with a Sinkhorn-style update, removes causal convolution, and extends matching from 3-grams to 4-grams.
mHC reorders residual mixing across layers, reducing estimated I/O from (4n+4)d to (3n+2)d.

✅ The larger pattern
DeepSeek is not merely compressing an existing model. It is willing to discard its own previous components when a cheaper system-level design emerges.
V4.1 Flash is less a smaller V4 than a new answer to one question: how much intelligence can be delivered per byte of memory and unit of inference cost?

🔗 Full analysis:
https://t.co/UToM7xMAgH

text:
In the last several years AI has progressed rapidly but predictably, and in that time the cyber community learns the bitter lesson over and over again. We’ve collectively sleep walked into the current state of things and now I see emotionally driven responses when those outside the community try to address it. “Do nothing” and continuing down the same path isn’t a counter proposal.

These models are far more capable and scaleable than any of us. And they cannot be deterred like a human adversary. Why would we reject the possibility that an agentic swarm could take down vast swaths of the internet, including critical infrastructure? This is rather ironic considering I've seen virtually no push back to L0pht's Senate testimony 28 years ago (or any of the panels celebrating its anniversary since) where they claimed they could take down the internet in 30 minutes.

We all know how broken things are, how so many in leadership never respond beyond moral support despite the overwhelming evidence. I'm no AI doomer, quite the opposite, but the current state of cyber stands in the way of realizing all of AI's benefits. The old way isn't going to work anymore and its time to abandon it. Abandon the complex risk management spreadsheets, the performative training, the compliance regimes, and yes remove humans in the loop for every decision. None of this will survive the speed and sophistication of agents driven by frontier models.

author: DefiFarmerYue
quoted_text:
$INTC 需求跑得比制造改善更快

这两天英特尔的信息挺密集。一边是陈立武最新的AI Infra Summit 谈话，一边是卖方更新的一批供应链数据。放在一起看，我之前一直跟踪的 Server CPU、18A、EMIB-T——都有了新的进展

1. Server CPU 现在是真的缺货

陈立武这次直接给了一个很夸张的数字：英特尔目前只能满足客户约 50% 的 CPU 需求，甚至已经有多位科技巨头 CEO 亲自打电话来要更多 CPU，他只能跟对方道歉：“我造得还不够多。”

他把这波需求明确指向 Agentic AI。随着 AI 从训练走向大规模推理和 Agent，编排、控制流、多线程任务都需要更多 CPU。之前从 Dell、HPE 的财报里已经看到传统服务器需求明显增长，现在英特尔自己也直接确认了供不应求

最新卖方供应链数据刚好补上制造端：Clearwater Forest 良率从 6 月约 20% 提升到目前约 50%，今年底开始小量生产，2027 Q1 全面生产，2027 年中再由 Diamond Rapids 接棒

所以Server CPU需求增长已经完全跑到了英特尔产能爬坡前面

2. 18A 的大芯片良率改善速度可观

最新供应链数据给出的 Panther Lake 18A 良率约 80%，Clearwater Forest 约 50%。Clearwater Forest 是面积更大的 Server CPU，6 月据说还只有约 20%，短短几个月已经拉到 50%

陈立武这次还讲了一个挺有意思的细节。刚接手英特尔时，他把 Fab 的真实数据开放给设备厂商，对方 CEO 看完以后直接告诉他初始良率“糟糕至极”，他的回答是：“这就是为什么我要找你们帮忙。”

英特尔以前很多制造问题喜欢关起门自己解决，现在开始把真实数据摊开，让设备商一起参与改善。至少从最近 18A 的数据看，这个办法似乎开始有效了

3. EMIB-T 最担心的良率，也有起色了

卖方最新拿到的日本基板厂数据是：Q2 20–25% → 目前约 45% → 9 月底目标 >50% → 明年 1 月约 55%。

Google TPU、AWS Trainium 等项目的供应链信号已经越来越多，如果后面真的进入百万级 AI ASIC 出货，英特尔必须把基板良率和有效产能一起拉起来。现在从 20% 多做到 45%，之前比较担心的制造瓶颈已经出现明显改善

卖方甚至已经把英特尔 Backend 收入预测做到 2027E $1.1B → 2028E $7B。这个预测很激进，但也第一次比较直观地展示了 EMIB-T 如果大规模商业化，对英特尔收入可能有多大影响

陈立武这次又把先进封装放到了未来五年的核心位置，专门谈到基板供应、预付款锁产能和美国本土先进封装能力。客户、良率、供应链扩产这几条线现在开始慢慢对上了

4. 14A 的时间也出现了新变化

陈立武这次直接说 14A 明年 Q1 投产，而最新卖方供应链预测给出的产能路径是 2027 年底 6K WPM、2028 年底 24K WPM

这里我暂时还不会把“Q1 投产”直接理解成大规模客户量产，因为此前英特尔对 risk production / HVM 的口径有所不同。今年 10 月还有一个很关键的 0.9 PDK，接下来再看客户 tape-out、实际良率和产能

至少 14A 已经越来越接近可以用真实产品和客户项目验证的阶段了

5. 27 年 英特尔产能绝对是不够的

这轮更新整体让我更乐观一点：Server CPU 的需求比我之前想的还强，CWF 和 EMIB 基板良率也都在快速改善

陈立武说目前只能满足约 50% 的 CPU 需求，而卖方预计 18A 产能到 2026 / 2027 年底大约是 40K / 60K WPM，也就是明年增加约 50%。这部分产能还要同时分给 PC 和 Server。与此同时，CWF 明年 Q1 全面生产，Diamond Rapids 年中又要开始上量，英特尔自己也预计供应限制会持续到 2027 年

需求端还有新的增量。最新卖方供应链信息提到，NVIDIA 下一代 Rosa / Feynman head-node 可能采用英特尔 x86 CPU，而且据供应链反馈，不少 NVIDIA 客户更倾向继续使用 x86 CPU，而非 NVIDIA 自家的 CPU

所以我现在的判断是：27 年英特尔应该能明显多卖 CPU，但产能问题导致肯定是供不应求的

如果 Agentic AI 的 CPU 需求继续维持现在的强度，CWF / Diamond Rapids 又按计划上量，明年 Server CPU 能增长多少，直接取决于英特尔 18A 的有效产能爬坡速度

text:
how to actually get into humanoid robotics in 2026, and this is where the money actually is right now.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

start with ros 2. this is still the industry standard for communication, sensing, and control across nearly every real platform. don't jump straight to a humanoid, start on gazebo or webots, both free, both built for ros 2, both with strong documentation for a genuine beginner.

move into simulation before you touch real hardware. pybullet and mujoco for reinforcement learning specifically, mujoco is the actual physics engine behind a huge share of current humanoid locomotion research, deepmind and most academic labs run on it. isaac sim from nvidia if you want gpu accelerated, photorealistic perception work, free to download, and nvidia's own introduction to robotic simulations self paced course walks you through the exact ros 2 reference architecture.

learn vla models next, and treat this as mandatory, not optional. vision language action models are the actual shift that changed what's possible in the last two years, robots now take a spoken instruction, plan the motion sequence, and execute it, without task specific programming. if you're in robotics and haven't studied vla architecture yet, you're already behind where the field currently sits.

hardware is more accessible than people assume. the so 101 robot arm, an open source platform, costs roughly $110 to build and has a genuinely active github ecosystem, teleoperation, imitation learning, and rl training all documented and reproducible. this is the actual entry point most self taught people are using right now, not a $20,000 humanoid.

understand the two training methods actually being used at the frontier. imitation learning, where a robot watches human demonstration data, motion capture or teleoperation, and distills it into a policy. reinforcement learning, where the robot discovers a strategy through trial and error in simulation, tesla uses this specifically for balance, gait, and grip force problems too hard to demonstrate perfectly by hand. tesla's own digital dreams approach takes one real demonstration and generates 10,000 synthetic variations with realistic physics, solving the actual bottleneck in this field, you cannot physically demonstrate every scenario at the scale training requires.

the honest state of the industry right now. figure 02 already completed a 20 hour continuous shift. tesla optimus runs a full 8 hour workday on its current battery. boston dynamics electric atlas is live in hyundai plants. this moved from research demo to real deployment in the last year, and the field is hiring specifically for the ros 2 plus vla skill combination right now.

start on ros 2 and a free simulator this week. move to a $110 arm before you need a $20,000 humanoid. study vla architecture like it's the actual frontier, because it is.

text:
The real AI bottleneck is moving from model capability to trusted execution in messy enterprise workflows.

Agents need context, permissions, evals, data boundaries, and verifiable actions. 
That “applied layer” is where a lot of durable AI infrastructure will be built.
author: MetisL2
quoted_text:
There’s a massive chasm between the power of AI models and the ultimate workflows that enterprises are trying to automate. This gap is the opportunity for the applied AI layer to fill. 

You need to connect the intelligence to workflows, often reengineer processes, aggregate the right context and data, allow for the right human in the loop experiences, drive change management, do domain specific evals, manage the security and governance of the data and process, and much more.

We’re going to see this layer emerge in every vertical and horizontal category. And ironically, even as models improve at incredible rates, this layer still must exist - and may become even more important and useful. Greater capability enables even more complex tasks to be tackled, amplifying the challenges if you don’t do this well.

Was super fun chatting with @sonyatweetybird on all the things going into AI diffusion.

text:
越来越精彩了，达里奥顶着特朗普干😲

特朗普前脚刚在电话里把AI 末日论称为骗局，还对黄仁勋说美国不会让 AI 减速。

不到 48 小时，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 就在旧金山 Dreamforce 上再次主张AI放缓迭代速度。

他的三步很明确：AI 公司提高透明度、加大安全投入，整个行业建立共同安全标准；最后再做国际协调。最核心的一句话也没变——如果你连自己产品的能力和安全都没把握，那就先别发，放慢一点，直到有把握。

黄仁勋这次则把另一派的逻辑讲得很清楚：

不需要新的法律和监管，创新速度和安全本来就不是二选一。企业应该尽可能快跑，真发现产品不安全、公司快失控了，再暂停解决。

关于AI的争论，可比币圈的某些瓜精彩多了，这才是所有人值得关注的话题。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
卧槽，Anthropic 既当又立？被人扒了精光😲😲😲

Dustin Moskovitz 2021 年就是 Anthropic 的早期投资人。后来他把这笔 Anthropic 股权捐进自己的慈善体系，2025 年 Forbes 估值大约 5 亿美元。

按后来披露的持股上限算，随着 Anthropic 估值暴涨，这笔资产理论价值最高已经接近 77 亿美元。

然后有意思的地方来了。

Moskovitz 的 Good Ventures、Coefficient Giving 以及相关捐赠渠道，又长期给一批 AI Safety 机构出钱。这里面包括 METR、Redwood 等安全研究和评估组织，也包括 Tarbell 这种专门培养 AI 记者的项目。

Tarbell 的学员后来进入 TIME、The Verge、LA Times 等媒体，持续报道 AI 风险；METR 则负责给 Anthropic、OpenAI 等前沿模型做“第三方安全评估”。

于是整个链条变成了这样：

Anthropic 越值钱 → Moskovitz 捐出的 Anthropic 股权越值钱 → AI Safety 圈子得到的钱越多 → AI 可能失控、需要更强监管的研究和舆论越多 → 政府越需要所谓独立第三方评估 → METR 这类机构权力越大。

偏偏最近 Dario Amodei 又开始推动嵌入式第三方评估者，甚至直接把 METR 当成例子。也就是说，未来这些机构可能不只是写报告，而是真正进入实验室，决定哪些模型太危险、哪些公司应该被限制。

这就是 Kevin Bass 今天为什么直接要求美国国会调查。

他指控的不是Anthropic 偷偷给 METR 打钱买结果，因为目前没有这种证据。真正的问题是：出钱的人、被评估的公司、负责评估风险的人、传播 AI 末日叙事的人，居然长期生活在同一个资金和人脉网络里。

甚至连人员都在互相流动。Anthropic 安全团队的人可以去 METR，Redwood 可以拿同一批资金，又给 METR 做调查分包。

早期 Anthropic 投资人和观察员，同时又出现在这些 AI Safety 组织的资金侧。

说白了，这就像一家制药公司的早期股东发了大财，然后这笔钱又去资助药品安全机构、医学媒体和监管研究，最后这些机构还被建议成为“独立裁判”。

即使每个人都没有作弊，这个结构本身也已经够别扭了。

Kevin Bass 把它叫做“监管捕获机器”：

先告诉所有人 AI 很危险
再资助研究证明 AI 很危险
再培养媒体不断讨论 AI 很危险
最后推动政府建立更重的监管

然后让同一个圈子里的机构负责评估谁有资格继续训练 AI。

text:
Started testing a looping strategy on @ZestProtocol to farm some of their new incentive campaign.

Here's what I've been doing:

• Supplied ~$92 of $sBTC
• Borrowed 30 $USDCx against it
• Swapped the USDCx into more $sBTC
• Supplied that sBTC back into Zest
• Repeated with another 10 $USDCx

Final position:

• $133 $sBTC supplied
• 40 $USDCx debt
• $93 net equity

Zest is now paying 0.5 BTC per month in incentives in $STX.

Half goes to $sBTC suppliers, while the other half goes to $USDCx borrowers with 20%+ LTV.

So the loop potentially lets me increase my sBTC exposure while earning incentives on both the supply and borrow side.

Of course, leverage cuts both ways.

A 10% rise in sBTC adds roughly $13 to my supplied position before interest and fees. A 10% drop does the opposite while also pushing my LTV higher.

Anyone running other loops on Zest?

Disclosure: I’m a long-time Stacks supporter and $STX holder.

'Inflation = bad' is taken as gospel today, but it ignores the fact that....

1) 'inflation' can mean a million different things, as every product or asset is constantly going up or down in price, and

2) 'inflation' in terms of goods and labor going up in price is almost impossible to separate from positive organic economic growth, ESPECIALLY in an economy like ours in which the currency is being actively debased at the same time...

And- as @hkuppy points out- economic growth is the main thing most actual real on the ground Americans are concerned about- not inflation.  

In this regard- while it might sound odd- I actually think most Americans would be happier with 10% wage growth and 10% inflation vs 2% wage growth and 1% inflation...

Yes- the math may be 'wrong'- but there's more to it than that...

The former scenario (high growth, high inflation) *feels* like there is opportunity and fluidity...

That if you work hard and pick the right career or business, and play your cards right, and manage your expenses, and think about the future, you can build wealth and ascend the ladder economically...

Whereas the latter scenario (low growth, low inflation) *feels* like everything is stagnant and calcified and ossified...

Like you are just going to be eternally punching in at globocorp like Sisyphus pushing the boulder up the hill, living in some Kafka-esque Office Space blue light hellscape, never getting ahead, always treading water, while rich boomers play golf all day and vote themselves more Medicare and SS and general all-purpose gibsmedat.

You gotta create an environment economically where normal average people feel like hard work and risk-taking are +EV... the whole 'virtuous cycle' concept... and this obsession with keeping inflation at 2% seems very much contrary to that at this point...

一文解析“孙宇晨奖”：全球首个以「题目清单」为核心的去中心化学术悬赏机制！

2026 年 9 月 16 日，波场 TRON 创始人孙宇晨宣布设立「孙宇晨奖」。以基础数学重大突破与机器形式化验证为唯一发奖标准，定位为「AI 时代的诺贝尔奖」，回应诺贝尔奖体系长期缺失数学奖项的历史空白。

孙宇晨自述其财富根源于密码学与数学，设立该奖是为「从数学中来，回到数学中去」。公益重心自此全面转向该奖。此前其在科技、环保、灾害救援等领域累计捐赠近 4500 万美元。

一、定位与基本原则

1/ 奖跟着题目走，不跟着人走。 不等年会、不等提名、不等年龄、不设国籍与机构门槛。

2/ 唯一触发器： 机器将证明从第一行核验至最后一行，一步不差。通过后，奖金归属启动。

3/ 两栏署名： 一栏记「证明者」，一栏记「形式化者」（将人类可读证明搬进机器并通过验证的人）。两栏可为同一人，也可互不相识；人、AI、人用 AI 均可，不区分物种。同一名字可多次出现。

4/ 三大原则： 开放、公益、开源。问题清单、验证标准、证明与核验材料通过 GitHub 公开；奖金发放记录上链存证，永久可追溯、不可篡改。

题单一旦挂出即永久锁定：只增不减，钱只兑不退。题目写错也按约定支付，再重新挂单。孙宇晨仅负责题单上架与定价签字，不参与验证、评审、挂名与发钱。

二、核心机制

1/ 时间与资格边界

•  覆盖自 2026 年 1 月 1 日 起取得的数学进展。

•  上架前已解决、上架后才完成形式化验证的题目：证明者仍记名，奖金只付给形式化者，不为数学史补发。

•  数学界已接受但尚未形式化的题目，状态栏写「已证明，待形式化」——名字先挂，钱不动。谁完成机器核验，空栏落名，奖金归属启动。

•  只奖励清单题目的首个完成者；多人共同完成则按贡献分配。

2/ 奖金分配

•  解题者（证明栏）：总奖金的 70%

•  形式化验证者：30%

•  同一人同时完成解题与形式化：获全额

•  AI 系统亦可获奖，但须由自然人、法人或其书面授权代表作为申报主体与法定收款人

•  奖金以加密货币发放，获奖者须通过运营方规定的合规与身份核验（KYC）

3/ 治理结构

•  出资人：孙宇晨个人，仅任捐赠人与颁奖人，不参与评审。

•  学术委员会：由领先 AI 模型与领域专家组成；AI 委员提供初评与建议，组委会作最终决定。利益冲突成员回避。

•  公开记录仓库：GitHub 组织 TheJustinSunPrize，题库、候选、已公告获奖与核验证据分库管理。

•  奖池已打入区块链，地址与余额公开，出资人仅保留继续注资权，不可撤回。

三、题库与首期结果

公开题库现收录 1022 道问题（编号 JSP-000001 至 JSP-001022），覆盖数论、组合、图论、分析、几何、代数等，包含七大千禧年问题（黎曼猜想、P vs NP、BSD 猜想、霍奇猜想、三维纳维–斯托克斯存在性与光滑性、杨–米尔斯存在性与质量间隙、庞加莱猜想），以及哥德巴赫猜想、大量埃尔德什未解问题等。已解决题目仍保留，以便衔接后续形式化。

首期已公告 66 道题，分级为：
•  巅峰级 1 项
•  里程碑级 14 项
•  进展级 36 项
•  贡献级 15 项

最高奖 100 万美元 授予 OpenAI 研究团队，表彰其对「三维纳维–斯托克斯方程存在性与光滑性问题」的解决及形式化。据公开信息，证明由内部系统产生，形式化由 GPT-6 Astra 完成，并通过 Lean 验证。其他已表彰成果还包括森多夫猜想、埃尔德什互异子集和问题等。

除奖金外，获奖者获证书与奖牌：主体为铜材，表面镀 6 克纯金；正面为孙宇晨头像及中英文奖名，背面为人类探索宇宙雕刻。

四、参与路径与公开入口

•  官方介绍：https://t.co/P2DBk7uASE

•  公开记录与题库：https://t.co/Ctlx7MSAzx

•  可通过仓库 Issue 模板推荐题目、推荐获奖人、更正记录或提出异议

•  联系邮箱：thejustinsunprize@hejustinsun.com

提交须经 GitHub 提交并通过 Lean 等形式化核验；机器核验通过是进入评审的前置条件，核验本身不等于最终授奖或付款权。

一句话理解这套机制：
把「人类已经认下、机器尚未认下」的证明，做成一张带价码、可核验、可结算的施工图：名字归数学界，钱归机器，出资人两边都不沾。空着的那一栏，本身就是对全世界的召集。

NEAR Intents 交易量累计正式超过 300 亿美元。

300 亿这个数据很重要，但另一个更重要的是，它正在加速增长：

从零到 100 亿的交易量用了 14.5 个月
从 100 亿到 200 亿用了 4.5 个月
而 200 亿到 300 亿却用了 3.5 个月

与此同时，NEAR Confidential Intents 的TVL 也刚刚突破 7000 万美元，
触发 NEAR@3.33 第一轮快照。

什么是 NEAR@3.33 ？

它是一种里程碑奖励代币，
用户把钱放在 NEAR 隐私账户，并符合一些条件，就有机会获得空投。

这个奖励蛮有意思的，它把 TVL 和 $NEAR 的价格捆绑在一起，可以吸引资金进来。

那么什么时候可以解锁这个奖励代币呢？
当 $NEAR 连续 3 天的平均成交价维持在 3.33 美元或以上，

它就可以按照 1:1 转换成真正的 $NEAR 。

交易量起来了，
TVL 也跟上了，
那么币价是不是也要起飞了？
author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
$NEAR 虽然是有年纪的 L1 老币，但它绝对和那些落伍吃老本的老币不一样。

在上一个牛市， $NEAR 的卖点是速度快，手续费低，就是一条普通的 L1 。我也没特别关注它。

最近发现 $NEAR 搞了个非常硬核的跨链系统 NEAR Intents

你只需要给一个指令，比如说，今天我要用一个以太换去 SOL，系统会把这个需求发给不同的平台。它们会竞争报价，胜出者负责完成换币、跨链和结算。

你完全不需要自己挑跨链桥，把币跨来跨去，还得去交易所买 Gas 。直接省心省力。

其中，这个过程还可以无缝加入隐私执行层。
这个隐私层主要隐藏的是成交前的订单意图和执行过程，为了避免大额订单被别人抢跑。
想象一下，如果有一天你要卖掉1亿美元BTC并买入SOL。
如果订单提前暴露，市场完全可以先一步买入SOL，等你来抬他的轿。

目前 NEAR Intents 已经处理过的跨链交易已经超过 130 亿美元， 

今年还开始收手续费了，把交易量变成真正的收入。

如果现在再把 $NEAR 当成一条普通老公链，
那你大几率已经看走眼。
不过牛市才刚开启，一切还来得及。

text:
I think there’s a very good chance the $BTC cycle bottom is already in.

BTC has been holding up relatively well recently considering it has two major headwinds expected this week:

A potential interest rate hike and the U.S. CLARITY Act likely failing to pass.

Both seem largely priced in, with prediction markets putting the odds of a rate cut at ~92% and the CLARITY Act being rejected at ~83%.

We’ve also had plenty of bearish news lately, yet BTC continues to hold above the $76.5K support zone.

What makes me even more bullish is the strength of the recent move from $65K to $82K.

I don’t think this is simply a bull trap.

In both 2018 and 2022, once BTC started making such aggressive moves off the lows, it meant that the cycle bottom was already in.

It’s also quite telling that BTC spent many months hovering around the $58k-$60K region from February through August without breaking below it.

Speaking of the bear case, September has historically been BTC’s worst month for performance.

But even if we move lower, as long as BTC holds the $72K–$73K area, for me the bullish thesis remains intact, and I’ll be buying any big dips.

That $72k-$73k zone is particularly important for me not only because it's a strong support level, but its 200-day EMA is also at $73K, which BTC historically retests when it resumes the uptrend.

Unless we have a black swan event, such as an FTX-like event or a major stock market crash, I personally don't think that BTC will break below $72K again.

So I see BTC's downside as relatively capped while the upside is Valhalla.

That’s why I’m bullish and I have a lot of crypto exposure right now.

Either way, I’m playing the long game. Regardless of short-term price action, I believe quality coins will be trading significantly higher a year from now.

Let’s run it back 🫡

text:
I’ve been experimenting with a new thesis and vision for this coming bull run: building games and experiences that build communities.

Not overselling “amazing games” or pretending we’re building the next AAA title, but building cool games you can jump into when you’re bored af, have some fun, compete with others, and then leverage those games to create traction around NFT launches, token launches, and whatever else we decide to build.
Our goals will grow through ambition and new available technology.  

In the past, 99.9% of crypto projects that promised games were a total and absolute scam. They raised millions promising AAA games and then couldn’t even deliver an OK game. Huge promises, huge raises, years of development, and in the end most of them built absolute crap.

During this bear market I’ve spent over 1,000 hours vibecoding, trapped in my NASA office, learning, experimenting and developing websites, tools, and even a really nice but way too complex Roblox game. It took a ridiculous amount of time, but I learned a lot.

Now I feel like all those pieces are finally coming together, and @uglyonrobinhood is the first step for us Efrogs to take over RH.

A lot of people have been asking me about Efrogs, Efroglets, and CROAK. Efrogs and Efroglets will be back, and they will be part of this ecosystem outside Linea, just like we’re already doing with the board at @ThePondStreet.  Their visibility will increase again, especially Efrogs. OG's never die. 

Regarding CROAK, I love the token to the moon and back, but right now Linea is community-dead. If Linea comes back and starts genuinely supporting communities again, I believe CROAK can come back strong too. 

But right now, we all see the new opportunity on RH, and I think the Efrog vibes that made our project shine: positivity, community, innovation, and always trying new stuff can work incredibly well there.

So let’s bring those vibes to RH. 🐸

This week we start with something simple: go to https://t.co/Bsmtrjf5nu, play the game, test it, try to break it, and compete.  

10 Efrogs will go to the Top 10 UGLY runners this week.

Next week I’ll share the full announcement about UGLY token launch and, more importantly, the bigger vision behind what we’re building.

This is only the first step. You are early on this new adventure. 

Frogbless y'all. 🐸

真正的问题不是"加不加"，而是"加几次"。6月的点阵图显示联储预期2026年底利率中位数在3.8%，如果今晚加25bp，利率中点就到3.875%，已经接近全年目标了。所以今晚核心看点是：更新后的点阵图会不会暗示12月还有一次加息？

如果点阵图把年底利率预期上调到4.1%，就等于明说"还有一次"，如果维持在3.9%附近，那就是"加完这次看数据"。

现在10年期美债收益率已经突破5%，这是2007年以来最高水平。而标普500的Shiller CAPE比率接近2000年互联网泡沫破裂前的第二高位。

高利率+高估值，这组合在历史上从来不是好兆头。

更要命的是，AI基础设施投资对"资金成本"极其敏感，谷歌、微软、亚马逊这些AI云巨头，今年Capex动辄上千亿美元，利率每上升100bp，资本回收期就要多延后1-2年。

从历史数据来看:
• 美联储开启加息周期后，标普500前3个月平均跌2%
• 如果是快速连续加息(比如2022-2023那轮)，跌幅能到17%

科技股现在的逻辑是"AI叙事支撑高估值"，但一旦利率继续上行、而AI变现速度跟不上Capex增速，估值就会被市场重新定价。

加息杀的是现金流差、靠低成本融资续命的「故事型叙事」。当利率居高不下，流动性溢价收紧，大资金只会去抢夺最稀缺、最不可替代的硬资产。

但有一个板块，反而因为加息变得更值钱，能源电力股，这也是我们之前反复提及的方向。

逻辑很简单：AI用电需求是刚性的，而且供给缺口在扩大。

AI现在的物理瓶颈根本不是算法,也不是GPU数量,而是电力与电网容量。没有电，最先进的Blackwell芯片也只能放在仓库当摆设。

我们看看美国电力紧缺数据:
• 美国数据中心用电需求2025-2030预计翻倍
• 但电网扩容要3-5年
• 传统电网并网申请排队长达3-5年

这个缺口不会因为利率上升就消失，微软、亚马逊、Meta已经签了20年的电力采购协议，基本把核电站产能直接包圆了。

算力即电力。科技巨头的Capex正在被迫从"买芯片"转向"买电厂和建电网"。

📝为什么"能源+AI"是当前最硬的对冲兼进攻资产?

第一，抗通胀与防加息。能源具备天然的抗通胀属性，且数据中心的PPA长期购电协议锁定的是未来数年的高确定性现金流。

第二，供给刚性。电网审批墙导致"现场离网发电"与"核电直连"成为刚需中的刚需。

我梳理了一下，这条产业链中，我们十分看好的几家公司:

📍 离网发电(解决电网排队瓶颈)

• $BE  (Bloom Energy)：固体氧化物燃料电池。部署速度极快，可实现月级别的部署，是目前数据中心拿不到电网额度时的唯一救命稻草。Q2营收首次破$1B，同比增长166%，手上25GW订单储备相当于未来几百亿美元收入。他们的卖点是6-12个月装好发电，而电网要等3-5年。

• $FCEL (FuelCell Energy)：熔融碳酸盐燃料电池,主打发电+碳捕集,匹配低碳AI数据中心的ESG刚需。

📍 传统基荷与核电直连(最稀缺的24/7零碳电)

• $VST  (Vistra Corp)：北美核电与发电商龙头。拥有极为稀缺的核电直连资源,科技巨头签长期PPA的绝对首选。3809 MW核电产能锁定了亚马逊和Meta的20年合同,这是"印钞机级别"的现金流。

• $GEV (GE Vernova):燃气轮机与高压电网基础设施双巨头。统治基荷天然气发电与变电站关键设备。

📍 电网输配与最后一公里(干重活的垄断者)

• $PWR (Quanta Services):北美最大的电网EPC施工巨头,垄断了高压输电线路与变电站建设的技术劳动力。没有它,电厂的电根本送进不了数据中心。Backlog接近$50B,未来2-3年的活儿已经锁定。美国电网改造订单排到2030年都接不完。

📍 芯片级垂直供电(硬件层的物理极限)

• $VICR (Vicor):高密度电源模块龙头。垂直供电(VPD)技术直接解决千瓦级单芯片(如Blackwell/下一代GPU)的板载电阻损耗与发热瓶颈。Backlog暴涨145%,给AI芯片做"最后一寸"供电模块,产能严重不足,正在收购新厂房扩产。

这些公司的共同特点是:订单已经签了,收入可见性极高,而且不依赖"AI叙事"，他们提供的是AI运行的必需品,不是AI本身。

🤔加息对能源股的影响,跟科技股完全相反:

• 现金流确定性:20年PPA、$50B backlog,这些都是白纸黑字的合同,不是"预期"也不是"叙事"。利率上升反而凸显这种确定性的稀缺性。

• 资产重估:电力基础设施在供给紧张时会溢价。核电站、燃气轮机、电网设备,这些资产的重置成本极高,而且周期长，Vistra的核电站如果现在要重建,成本是当年的3-5倍。

• 通胀对冲:能源价格跟通胀正相关,而美联储加息恰恰是因为通胀压力没消退。能源股是天然的通胀对冲工具。

• 不依赖VC资金:科技股(尤其是AI初创公司)对风险资本高度依赖,利率上升会让VC融资萎缩;但能源股的客户是云巨头和政府,资金来源稳定。

总结来说，如果美联储今晚加息,且点阵图暗示12月还要再来一次,科技股大概率会继续承压，因为市场会开始担心"连续加息周期"。

但能源电力股反而可能迎来重估机会:
• 相对估值优势:科技股Shiller CAPE接近泡沫区间,而能源股很多还在历史估值中位数以下
• 防御属性:在加息周期里,投资者会从"成长股"转向"现金流稳定的价值股"
• AI基建的必需品:即使AI泡沫破了,数据中心该用的电还是得用，需求刚性不会变

市场现在还在用"AI繁荣→科技股永远涨"的线性思维,但忽略了一个事实:

AI繁荣的最大受益者,可能不是造AI的公司,而是给AI供电、建基础设施的公司。

就像淘金热时代,真正赚到钱的不是淘金者,是卖铲子和牛仔裤的人。

今晚美联储加息落地后,科技股可能会有1-2个月的调整期(历史平均跌幅2%,如果是连续加息周期可能更深)。

而能源电力股,现在可能是过去18个月里最被低估的时候，因为所有人都在追AI芯片和算力,没人关心"电从哪来"。

但等到某一天,某个云巨头因为电力不足推迟数据中心上线,市场才会意识到：能源基础设施才是AI时代真正的瓶颈。

但到那时候再买,就晚了。

在这场宏观重塑中,算力与电力的供需失衡,正把能源电力板块推向未来3-5年最硬核的alpha逻辑。在算力即权力的时代,掌控能源与变压器的人,才是真正收税的人，DYOR🙏

text:
“The problem is not that you were not educated. The problem is that you were educated just enough to believe what you were taught, and not enough to question everything you were told.” — Edgar Morin

Learning was meant to open the eyes. Too often it shuts mouths instead — other people’s, and one’s own.

One of the subtler instruments of cultural hegemony is education: not when it teaches ignorance, but when it teaches people to handle knowledge as authority. 

The mere use of what one has learned is not the harm. The harm begins when knowledge ceases to be a tool for seeing the world and becomes a closed system of belief, which the person will no longer allow to be questioned. The more elaborate the system of terms, the easier it is to fit new facts into the old scheme rather than admit that the scheme may be wrong.

A university once gave a person a measurable competence, a real range for growth — of the self, and of the field they worked in. Today it more often hands over a paper that certifies the right to invoke it. We may have mistaken schooling for education, and education for the collecting of diplomas.

Not because study is useless — universities have produced people whose work is a genuine starting point for those who come after. The trouble begins when a few years of study give too many people not knowledge so much as the feeling that they possess it. A handful of terms, a few canonical names, a couple of studies, and then the expert sentence: “science says.”

There is no need to say “this is what I think.” That is a dangerous sentence. Someone may think otherwise, and a door stays open for an argument in which one might have to admit a mistake, and the mistake would force a second look at the stance and the view attached to it. Easier to say “studies show,” and close the other person’s mouth.

“I was taught this, and it agrees with what I know — therefore it must be true.” Then a fact that contradicts the picture of the world no longer looks like a fact. It looks like an attack on identity. Conversation stops being a search for what is so. It becomes the defence of a position.

A diploma now certifies that someone attended a course of study in a chosen field. It does not certify that they learned to think through the field as a whole, nor through its ties to other disciplines and to the reality in which those disciplines sit.

Biology is brought in piecemeal to settle every difference — or to certify that there is none. Psychology accounts for every failure, because trauma explains everything. Sociology will find a culprit: the system, a theory, some scapegoat from a chosen era — instead of helping us see our own part in making the system, or in choosing which social theory to put to work. 

Science, instead of helping us understand and giving tools for the growth of a person and a society, supplies reasons to change nothing.

And when science confirms, with suspicious regularity, the stories that happen to be current, it is worth asking whether we are being taught to think and to mend the world — or how to fit ourselves into a society someone else has already designed.

This is not an attack on science. These are questions.

Morin wanted doubt taught — including doubt of our own doubts. Without that, knowledge does not push us forward. It only gives a more refined language, and a shield, for what is already comfortable. What remains is a footnote instead of a question.

In the mass rush for diplomas, I hope we do not run short of people who can still say: “And what if what I think I know is only the beginning of the discussion?”

author: coinalyzetool
quoted_text:
Researchers argue LLMs don't actually understand anything.

They call it "Potemkin Understanding."

For years, we’ve evaluated AI using human tests. The Bar Exam. AP Tests. The MMLU.

When a model aces these tests, we assume it understands the concepts. Because if a human passes the test, they fundamentally understand the material.

But that assumption is fatally flawed.

Humans make predictable mistakes. When we misunderstand something, there is a logical pattern to our errors.

The researchers discovered that AI does not fail like a human.

It fails like an illusion.

They ran an experiment. They asked top models to define complex concepts from game theory, literature, and psychology.

The AI nailed the definitions perfectly.

Then, they asked the AI to do something simple: identify a real-world example of the exact concept it just defined.

Performance completely collapsed.

Even worse, when researchers asked the AI to generate a custom example, the AI later failed to correctly classify its own generated output.

The models were fundamentally incoherent.

They exhibited up to a 62% failure rate the moment they had to actually apply the knowledge they just flawlessly defined.

The models aren’t reasoning. They are just reciting memorized patterns wrapped in a conversational tone.

The researchers named it after a Potemkin village, a fake, hollow facade designed to look impressive from the outside, with absolutely nothing behind it.

Every major AI company is selling you intelligence based on benchmark scores.

But this paper proves those benchmarks are a mirage.

For ONyc holders & reinsurance yield investors, this year's historically quiet Atlantic Accumulated Cyclone Energy (ACE) is a welcomed tailwind🤞

ACE is a measure of a season's total cyclone activity, calculated by summing the squares of each named storm’s maximum sustained winds every six hours so that stronger, longer-lived storms count more than weak, short-lived ones.

Lower ACE in the Atlantic could translate to lower insurance losses, & higher loss-adjusted reinsurance yields. 

ACE as of Sep 10 is *93% below normal*, and we are just about to pass the climatological peak for hurricane seasons. If the trend holds, it could be an exceptional calendar year for reinsurance investors

quoted_text:
An audit is a snapshot. The codebase keeps moving after it — upgrades, permission changes, new integrations — and every diff quietly reopens the attack surface. Meanwhile the attackers probing it are increasingly agents themselves: tireless, parallel, always on. A once-a-year PDF was never going to hold that line.

That's the bet behind @ZeroDriftSec: security that runs continuously and acts at machine speed — detect the risk, prove it's actually exploitable, ship the fix. The name is literal: zero drift between what your code intends and what it does.

I've watched @Normanxbt and his team live this bet. Their Season 3 application was rejected — sharp idea, not enough traction yet. They didn't argue with the feedback. They came back for S4 with paying clients, whitehat containments backed by onchain receipts, and their AI auditor working inside real audit engagements. That's what earned the conviction. The full story is theirs to tell — Norman's write-up is coming.

Proof of work, not promises. Proud to have them in our @EASYResidency S4.

quoted_text:
币圈里能一直跟的人极少。神鬼蛇神太多，话能信一半已经算客气。我目前真正认的，就两个：黑鬼 Ansem（@blknoiz06），以及王大有，现在大家叫他王小有（@youyou5202）。

不是因为他们从不说错。是因为他们说出来的东西，多数是自己先想过、自己先押过、也愿意把逻辑摊开的，不是随手丢一个币过来等着接盘。

---

黑鬼 Ansem：我是看他一路走过来的

公开履历很清楚。Zion Thomas，X 上是 @blknoiz06，CoinDesk 2024 最具影响力名单里被写成 Memecoin King。早期在 SOL 大概 1.5 美元附近重仓并扛过 FTX 后的至暗，后来又早站 BONK、WIF。市场上常被引用的倍数是 BONK 约 80 倍、WIF 约 520 倍——具体仓位因人而异，但方向和时机是看得见的。

他不是只会喊 meme。后来做 TCG Crypto 研究、和人一起做 Bullpen，还上 Market Bubble 聊预测市场。2026 年社区围绕他名字出来的 $ANSEM（Black Bull）把影响力又推了一层：有人空投、有人跟叙事、也有人质疑筹码集中。这些争议本身说明一件事——市场在拿真金白银给他的名字定价。

我对他也怀疑过。币圈谁没怀疑过。到现在我没在他身上吃过大亏。认真听过、跟过的，里面确实有单币走出百万市值级别的行情。不是每条推都是圣旨，是他判断叙事和流动性的手感，比大多数喊单号稳。

---

王大有 / 王小有：推荐之前，他先替你想过一遍

中文区里，他不是那种天天丢合约地址的人。早年 Venus 亚太、Xterio 顾问，2020 年就开始在币乎、微博写东西。真正让更多人记住他的，是 ArbDoge AI（$AIDOGE）：先匿名把项目做到约 2 亿美元市值，再实名站出来认。项目方当时也确认他是创始人和领导者。市值后来回落是事实，但“匿名做到高点再露脸、把责任接过来”这件事，和割完就跑的玩法不是一类。

后面还有 HODL、ZOO OF MEME、JAGER 等他参与或推动的社区叙事。他自己也反复讲过：团队仓怎么拿、空投真不真、有没有老鼠仓，愿意把过程写出来，甚至为社区对赌股权。最近还有社区拿“黄牛 / Yellow Bull”跟他绑定，本质还是同一套——人先在，币才有故事。

他推的东西，观感上是整理过的项目，不是随手发一个等着收割。币圈割韭菜的人太多了，能把逻辑、仓位和责任写清楚的人很少。

---

为什么只认这两个人

一个是英文区把 Solana 叙事和 meme 流动性吃透的交易员，一个是中文区从写稿、做项目到带社区都肯露脸的人。路径不同，共同点只有一个：不是纯嘴炮。

所以我的态度很简单——

如果你也认他们，就少听噪音，坚定持有你真正理解过的仓位。不是无脑梭哈每一条推，是在他们已经替市场想过一轮的方向上，给自己留时间。

币圈不缺神棍，缺的是还能对上号的人。黑鬼和大有哥，是我目前还能对上号的两个。

gm @pendle_fi fam - sharing a complete breakdown of the Penconomics dashboard, section by section (starting with Balances and more to follow soon).

At the top is the total sPENDLE redistributed to stakers, bought on the market. The bar chart is one bar per epoch. Hover or tap a bar for more details and the tx.

The three figures under it, all in PENDLE terms and annualised:

1. Plain sPENDLE APR, latest epoch: what a plain staker earned in the most recent distribution.

2. Boosted APR, average locker: what a vePENDLE locker earned, at the average boost across locks. Every lock has a different time left, so every boost is different; this is the average.

3. Same payout, sPENDLE only, no boost: the latest payout spread over sPENDLE holders alone, as if the locked PENDLE weren't there. That's where plain APR heads once the boost runs out (Jan 2028), if unlocking PENDLE isn't restaked.

The Fed decides at 2pm ET. Some context first.

On Aug 14, odds of a September hike:
- @Polymarket : ~53%
- CME futures: ~33%
Today:
- @Polymarket: ~89%
- CME futures: ~93%
Polymarket was pricing the September hike much earlier than Fed funds futures.

September is basically settled. October isn't:
· Polymarket: ~36%
· CME futures: ~47% (implied from CME's rate-range probabilities)
The side that was more hawkish🦅 in August is now the more dovish🕊️ one?

The number that actually matters today is the new median 2026 year-end dot.
In June the Fed printed 3.8%. If they hike this afternoon, 3.8% stops being possible.

3.9% → one and done
4.1% → one more before year-end
4.4% → two more before year-end

Our call: 4.1%.

The question is whether this is a hike, or the start of a hiking cycle. What's your call? 🤔

text:
分发即是一切。
谁掌握了用户，谁就掌握了话语权。

放眼整个 Crypto 行业，真正称得上“入口”级的存在，从始至终只有两类。
▌中心化交易所 - 以 Binance 和 Coinbase 为代表，掌握真正意义上的分发霸权。
▌稳定币发行商 - 以 Tether 和 Circle 为代表，虽然不直接面向 C 端，却是资金流动的底层管道。

其他所谓入口，大多只是短暂的流量幻觉。

1/ Telegram: 最像入口的非入口
坐拥 10 亿用户的 Telegram, 被视为理论上最强大的分发渠道。但结局并不如人意。
从“点一点小游戏”到成为真实的链上用户，这中间的漏斗过于陡峭，用户转化始终没能兑现。

2/ CEX 的霸权，正在被链上入口蚕食
以 Hyperliquid 为代表的 Perp DEX  正在直接切走 CEX 最核心的那块蛋糕。合约是 CEX 的利润引擎，Perp DEX 的崛起是对其商业模式最致命的一次冲击。
链上交易平台正在蚕食现货交易。以 FOMO 为代表的新一代链上社交产品，正在承接 Meme 币以及那些 CEX 根本上不了的长尾资产。所幸目前蚕食的量级还不算大。

FOMO 传送 - https://t.co/WN2bCgwGmM

3/ CEX 不会死，但它正在降级
CEX 当然不会消失。但它正从 Crypto 世界最大的入口慢慢退化。
真正的交易入口、发现入口、投机入口，正在被链上产品一点点瓜分蚕食。

text:
Catena is live on @Arc from day one.

Catena is a new kind of financial platform for AI-operated businesses and their agents. It brings together accounts, fiat and stablecoin money movement, agent identity, policies and controls, assurance protection, and a complete evidence trail in one system.

Starting today, Catena customers can convert fiat into USDC, hold it in their Catena accounts, and send it on Arc mainnet. Agents can also make governed payments that settle on Arc under Catena’s multi-rail policy and approval controls, with evidence that can be reviewed and verified afterward.

Stablecoins move value across borders almost instantly at low cost. For agents, that is useful, but it is only part of the story.

Just as importantly, stablecoins make money movement programmable, with rules encoded in the movement itself rather than applied at the edges. This gives AI safety constraints real force and creates evidence that can be independently verified.

Stablecoins do not make agents safe by default. But even if an agent becomes misaligned, it cannot bypass authority that is enforced cryptographically outside the AI.

That is the difference between giving an agent money and giving it governed access to banking across multiple payment rails. Rules are enforced before and during execution, and every action leaves a record that can be verified and audited afterward.

The evidence trail does more than make agent activity auditable. It also creates the foundation for a new kind of protection for agent payments. More on that soon.

Arc makes programmable stablecoins more powerful with a network designed specifically for fast, predictable financial activity. It is an open, EVM-compatible Layer 1 built for financial markets, real-time money movement, and agentic economic activity.

An agent should not need to acquire or manage a separate volatile token just to spend dollars. Arc uses stablecoins as gas, no other token needed.

An agent should not have to guess at network fees. Arc provides predictable, dollar-based fees.

An agent should not have to wait days, hours, or even minutes for a payment to settle. Arc provides deterministic sub-second finality.

Arc is purpose-built for stablecoin payments and financial markets, rather than for every possible on-chain use case. Its design is intended to keep financial activity from competing with unrelated speculative traffic for capacity.

Arc’s architecture is also designed to support privacy for sensitive financial activity alongside the compliance and reporting requirements of financial institutions.

Arc provides financial infrastructure for programmable money. Catena provides the financial platform businesses need to put that money to work through agents while keeping control.

Money for Agents. Control for You.

Explore Arc: https://t.co/kCWGbH4IKy

this work from Google engineers is pure f*cking treasure

they built WikiSkill: a system that turns an agent's execution history into persistent knowledge, then compiles it into reusable skills

this is basically an experience compiler for agents

the loop:

run tasks ➜ preserve raw traces ➜ consolidate recurring failures + successful strategies into a wiki ➜ propose one atomic skill update ➜ validate ➜ keep or rollback

the clever part:

skills can roll back
the wiki never does

successful strategies, recurring failures, rejected edits and skill impact history survive into the next iteration

the result is f*cking amazing

my takeaway:

the next agent memory layer should distill experience into procedures an agent can execute, validate and transfer

raw traces ➜ persistent knowledge ➜ validated skills ➜ a better next run

SBPFv3 is the new bytecode format, ready to integrate into your Solana programs now.

SBPFv3 resolves syscalls at compile time, enforces a strict ELF layout, and aligns Solana with upstream eBPF. 

Solana no longer maintains a bespoke bytecode dialect.

Down the road, SIMD-0500 makes SBPFv3 the only deployable format. Its feature gate ships in the next Agave v4.4 release, so the best time to migrate is now.

The toolchain is ready and rebuilding is a few commands for most Rust programs.

quoted_text:
昨天看 @0xBeyondLee 老师盘点 @EASYResidency，写得太全面了。

新一期 S5 马上开幕，而且就在泰国。作为第二季项目方，我来聊几个大家最关心的问题：

怎么加入 EASY Residency，入选后是什么体验，以及它到底对项目有什么帮助。

怎样加入 EASY Residency

加入 EASY，意味着你成为 @yzilabs 的被投项目，也就是某种意义上的“CZ 门生”。

这并不容易，但也不是完全没有方法。

先说一句，以下主要针对 Crypto 项目。AI 和其他赛道我不懂，不乱讲。

1. 基本功

现在的 EASY Residency，可以理解成 @cz_binance 的“梦想基金”。

它的核心不是找下一个“百倍币”，而是找到有能力、有想法，而且愿意长期折腾的人。

币圈发展到今天，从起项目、做产品、TGE、上所、做市值、拉 TVL，已经形成了一套相对成熟的产业链。

真正稀缺的，是把这些环节都经历过、而且现在还在一线持续搞事的人。

这也是 YZi “投项目就是投人”的原因：

这个项目未必成功，但这个团队、这个人，大概率早晚会成功。

比如 S4 的 SmartX @David_MetaWorld、XAPI @0xAA_Science、Xhunt @DeFiTeddy2020；

S3 的牛子液体 @cryptoxiao、蝴蝶 @eth_cedric；

S2 的 Predict Fun @dingalingts。

这些人的共同点，不是追到一个风口，而是长期愿意在币圈折腾，主观能动性极强。

不是游客。

所以如果你自己的资历还不够强，组队的时候尽量把拼图补齐，会非常重要。

2. 产品准备度

这个很看赛道。

目前大多数 DeFi 类别的入选团队，基本已经有可用产品，有些甚至已经跑出了不错的数据。

比如 S4 的 @elfomo_fi、@XStableAI、@SmartXTerminal。

但也不是所有项目都要求做到这个程度。

比如 RWA，尤其支付类项目，牌照和合规本来就需要很长周期，不可能要求一蹴而就。

3. 与 YZi 投资策略的契合度

YZi Labs 每一期 EASY Residency 之前都会提前公布主题。

比如 S5 的主题是：

“AI inside markets” AI 如何改变不同市场里的交易逻辑。

所以如果你做的是 AI 提升交易策略、执行效率、市场分析等等，当然都很切题。

但这里有一个问题：

谜底写在谜面上的方向一般都是最卷的。

每一期都会收到大量为了“切题”让 GPT 临时拼出来的项目，然后被批量过滤。

YZi 也不会希望 Demo Day 连着十几个一模一样的项目。

所以你需要顺着主题再挖一层。

如果“AI inside markets”真的成为新常态，那么市场里的发行、交易、做市三类参与者，行为会发生什么变化？又会产生什么新的需求？

能把场景给出来，再点出场景的刚需，那么只要场景值得“赌”，成功率就会高一截。

入选后的体验

EASY Residency 不是黑客松。

入选项目后，先是 5 周线上培训，导师会覆盖立项、发币、Pitch、GTM 等各个环节。

我们当年这一段是在新山 Network School。

一声叹息。

然后进入 5 周线下集训，一直到最后的 Demo Day。

我个人感觉，S4 比 S2 的线下共建更有生产力。

原因也很简单：

大家被“困”在不丹首都，周围没什么别的可干，只能每天集中精力想项目、搞建设。

在这一点上，EASY 团队表示：“选廷布这样‘清真’的城市真是太棒了，下次还干。”

Demo Day 的规格一般也很高。

YZi 会请很多知名机构负责人、大 KOL 现场听 Pitch。

比如这次有 1KX 的 @pet3rpan_  Capital 的 @arthur0x  Spartan 的 Kelvin Koh、DCG 的 @BarrySilbert  Dragonfly @tomhschmidt 等等。

甚至不丹国王也亲临现场。

所以 S4 可能也是历史上第一批直接对着国家元首 Pitch 的 Crypto 项目方。S5 Demo Day和Binance Blockchain Week同期举办，想必阵仗也不会小

实际上对项目有什么帮助？

简单说三点。

1. 冷启动

YZi 有时会直接牵头，帮项目在 EASY Residency 的毕业生网络里做第一波增长。

比如 @xhunt_ai 那次 Echo 活动。

同时 YZi 自己也会围绕 EASY 做不少曝光。

如果利用得好，至少可以帮你省掉一部分 Twitter 从 0 做到 3000 粉的冷启动成本。

2. 快速建立 VC 网络

整个 Program 会帮你接触很多机构和 Angel。

比如 S4 的 Sandeep 就相当积极。

当然有一说一，作为华人项目方，最后想真正 close 北美的钱，依然不容易。

EASY 能帮你把门打开，但不能替你把 cheque 拿回来。

3. 背书

这个其实最简单。

做过市场的人都知道：

有 YZi，和没有 YZi，完全是两回事。

如果你觉得自己是那块料，记得迅速申请参战：

https://t.co/imFxkcuXUJ

如果你申请了但是吃不准：

欢迎私信我，老中医免费给你支几招。

author: businessbarista
quoted_text:
My friend called me and asked the best way to set up personal agents for his daily life. So I made this video for him.

It takes you from zero to agents running, using the easiest and best 24/7 agent harness right now. All for $20 a month.

I already have tons of them running my personal life. One buys my groceries. One reads my email. One sends me something to learn every morning at 8 AM.

Here's the walkthrough, from easy mode to god mode.

Easy Mode: what @GrokBot actually is

Definition: a chat with a computer behind it. Grok Bot (from @cursor_ai and xAI) spins up one virtual machine in the cloud. Every bot you build shares it, and it stays on when your laptop is closed.

Two things to know:

1) It starts at a $20 a month Cursor Pro plan. It used to need the $300 tier.

2) Give every bot one job and a name. Mine is Barry. He's my personal assistant and he checks on the other bots every hour.

Hard Mode: giving your bots a credit card, an inbox, and a phone.

Definition: the stuff a bot needs to actually do things in the real world, not just talk about them.

Rules of thumb:

1) Payments. Don't put your credit card on the VM. It's beta. Use the Stripe Link CLI instead, so the card never sits on the machine. Then add a hard rule that the bot needs your yes before any purchase.

2) Email. Give your bot its own address. I use Agent Mail (free). Sign up for new services with it, send your junk there, and let the bot triage every six hours and only ping you when something needs a reply.

3) Phone. Give your bot a number and it can make reservations, call vendors, and take calls for you. I haven't set mine up yet, but people are already doing it.

God Mode: the fleet

Definition: a channel where your bots talk to each other and you only talk to the lead.

Rules of thumb:

1) Keep your bots small and specific to each task. Have an orchestra bot to help coordinate the rest.

2) Long threads plus frequent routines burn credits fast. Have each bot write a daily summary to one channel, then have your lead bot read that one channel instead of every conversation.

Full walkthrough: https://t.co/vDWnB24dne

text:
Did you miss the early Robinhood runners?

There could be another chance to run it back.

@arc mainnet goes live today.

Here are 6 projects I’m watching before the timeline catches up:

1. Tolly ($TOLLY): Launchpad + trading terminal

@TollyLabs combines a launchpad, a trading terminal and onchain analytics. It has already done roughly $4.9M in volume across 46K trades.

Part of the fees goes toward $TOLLY buybacks and burns, with around 28.9M TOLLY already removed from circulation.

2. Long ($LONG): Stock-paired memecoin launchpad

@Longdotsupply wants to pair memes with tokenized stocks, taking the Robinhood stock / meme experiment onto Arc.

I find this more interesting than another standard meme launcher, though it depends on whether tokenized stocks actually gain traction on the chain.

3. Arguspad ($ARGUS): Memecoin launchpad

@Arguspad is a straightforward memecoin launchpad. I’m watching whether it starts producing actual runners.

One or two successful launches can change where traders spend their time, but I’d want to see that happen before getting too excited about $ARGUS.

4. Warp ($WARP): Cross-chain USDC launchpad

@circlewarp combines a launchpad and trading terminal with cross-chain USDC transfers through CCTP.

The appeal is being able to move USDC from another chain and trade tokens on Arc without going through three different apps.

5. Archemist: X-based token launcher

@Archemistdotfun lets you launch tokens through an X bot. Its V4 setup includes anti-snipe mechanics, creator buys, buybacks and holder rewards.

I’m curious how the anti-snipe mechanics work in practice once people are trading with real money.

6. ArcDEXScan: Scanner + aggregator

@ArcDEXScan combines a scanner, aggregator and launchpad. This is one I’d keep open even without buying anything through it.

If launches end up spread across 20 different venues, having somewhere to see what’s moving would save a lot of digging.

For the first few days, I’d stick to official Arc / USDC routes once they’re live, use a fresh wallet and avoid unlimited approvals.

I wouldn’t try to guess Arc’s $PONS before the market opens. I’d rather see which venues get real volume and whether their launches hold up.

Anyway, this is a "watchlist" and not recommendation to buy.

Market's tanking + new chain + early stage projects = high risk.

text:
hype-free explanation of jev:

jev does not replace gpt / claude

jev is just a *really* smart switch statement

like if 2016 ml classifiers got 2026 levels of intelligence

it's a new* type of tool that will make a lot of workloads insanely fast, cheap, and accurate

* = and by new, i mean rebranded

~~~

it needs a predefined set of options and it will tell you which one to take

it cannot:

- write code
- generate natural language
- reason step by step / show its work
- produce any output you didn't define in advance
- pick from more than ~255 options in one shot

but it can:

- classify, route, score, rank
- give confidence
- pick the right branch, tool, model, or sub-agent
- judge / verify / guardrail an llm's output
- label tons and tons of rows

~~~

i'd imagine a lot of workflows that look like:

llm proposes options → jev decides → code executes

and i see this fitting *really* well with code mode and mcp

~~~

implying this will lead to agi seems incredibly far fetched to me, but i don't want to discount the types of applications that this will make possible

text:
真实实验太贵怎么办？

先让 Agent 在自己的历史轨迹里「做梦」几百遍，再决定下一步把算力花在哪里。

这篇 Dream-RSI 做的就是这件事。

每次真实探索后，系统会把走过的分支、失败方案、评测结果和计算成本保存成一棵 Discovery Tree。

这些历史随后被重组成一个 Replay Simulator。Agent 可以在里面低成本尝试新的搜索策略，比如先探索哪条路、什么时候并行、什么时候停止，而不用重新执行真实实验。

选出更好的策略后，再放回真实环境继续探索。新的轨迹又会进入模拟器，形成下一轮自我改进。

有意思的是，底层 Coding Agent 始终没变。

真正持续进化的是「怎么探索」这层策略。

实验覆盖算法设计、数学优化和 GPU Kernel。Lasso 任务里，相比 SimpleTES，Agent 调用最高减少约 162×；GPU Kernel 任务中，相同预算下最高获得 2.09× 性能提升。

所以 Agent 的历史轨迹可能远不止是 Memory。

只要把过去的分支、决策和结果保存得足够完整，它们也可以变成训练下一版探索策略的模拟环境。

有点像人做研究时在脑子里反复推演：

先想清楚哪条路更值得走，再真正动手做实验。

An archive node used to be all or nothing. In Nethermind 2.0 it's a question: how much history do you need?

All of it. Everything since a block you pick. A rolling window. Or the window plus named addresses from genesis.

An L2 that settles on @ethereum only needs state back to the end of its challenge window. Keep a month, let the rest age out.

Sync it from genesis, or stream our snapshot straight into the DB and have an archive serving in under a day. Either way the node checks what it holds against the block headers.

Needs the flat DB layout, the default in 2.0. Existing archives keep working as they are.

Also live on @gnosischain. Snapshots for both chains below.

text:
🐳 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，无奈之选

自从 GPT 给中文用户强行降智之后，之前买的 Pro 20x 已经被打入冷宫，纯属浪费钱还看着给自己添堵。

于是，抄起 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，看看到底能不能干活吧。

在官方的 DSH 框架 + 标准模式下，实际使用下来（DeFi 项目相关），我的感受是：

写代码能力基本够用，但智商可能不是很在线。

举个直观点的例子。

Jupiter 报价滑点失败的问题。

设置 10% 滑点，但是价格从：

0.025 SOL 能买 32,081 → 20,850 MEME Token。

你告诉我，这说明代币价格暴跌了 35%？！

那是暴涨了 35% 好吗，我滴乖乖。

除了这个，今天跟它沟通一个策略，前后花了几个小时，我发现 这个 V4.1 Flash 在很多策略层面上的理解都是错的，或严重偏离我的原始预期。

我只能不断的反复纠正它的错误观点。

这就搞得有点心累了。

我原以为 AI 除了写代码能力比我强百倍之外，在策略层面也应该面面俱到，既能高高拿起，又能轻轻放下的水平。

但这个 V4.1 Flash 却经常有犯蠢的时候，所以你肯定是不敢全权委托它给你搞策略的，何况涉及到资金到问题上。

前两天用 Fable 5.1，则全程基本处于：它说 xxx，我说对对对，按照你的计划来推进。

现在轮到我不断给 V4.1 Flash 纠正错误，但我脑子也不够用啊，我找 AI 不就是为了给我补脑子的吗？

至于前面为什么说代码能力还行，那是因为我把 GPT 6 Astra 写的代码给它分析，结果 V4.1 Flash 发现了 N 个问题，并一一修复了。

侧面证明 GPT 6 的降智得有多严重，多么不把中文用户当用户。

说起这个，能怪谁呢？

只怪疯狂蒸馏的国产之光的模型公司们了。

所谓：

前人种树，后人乘凉；

前人砍树，后人遭殃。

咱们就成了纯遭殃的中文 GPT 散户。

text:
孙宇晨北大那几届出了多少人才和奇葩？

看到孙割这个奖突然好奇查了一下，这几届太 TM 离谱了，尤其是孙宇晨的 2007 那一级，可以认为是“白金一代”

真正离谱的是北大 07 级数学。

北大官方的 2007 级数学本科名录里，王虹、苏炜杰、唐云清、孙鑫等确实都在；邓煜也是 2007 进入北大，后来转去 MIT。

到了 2026 年这一届已经出现：

王虹：菲尔兹奖
邓煜：菲尔兹奖
苏炜杰：考普斯奖
唐云清：国际一线数论学者
孙鑫：国际一线概率/数学物理学者

而且北大报道指出，这一届还有一批已经成为世界各高校教授的一线学者。也就是说，不是“这一届出了两个天才”，而是整个数学班出现了人才簇。

牛逼🐮
author: justinsuntron
quoted_text:
我为什么要设立孙宇晨奖

一
诺贝尔发明了炸药。他一生的财富，大部分来自这件东西。
据说1888年，一家法国报纸误发了他的讣告，标题叫"死亡商人死了"。他读到了自己的讣告，几年后立了遗嘱。
今天没有人再叫他死亡商人。
"诺贝尔"变成了一个中性的名词，像"伏特"和"瓦特"一样，不带感情，只是一个单位。他把钱交给"对人类做出最大贡献的人"，钱回到了人类手里，他的名字也随之回归中立，不是靠辩护，是靠一百多年的获奖名单。
我讲这个故事，是因为我理解他。我知道钱从哪里来，也知道钱可以去哪里。

二
我的财富，根源是数学。
区块链这个行业，整体建立在几个长期研究支撑的密码学构造与安全假设上：椭圆曲线上的离散对数难解，哈希函数不可逆，大数难以分解。1985年，两个数学家各自想到可以用椭圆曲线做密码，一个在大学，一个在IBM，互不相识。那年没有人觉得这件事有用。他们在黑板上写下的东西，后来变成了一个万亿美元的市场，变成了一种前所未有的东西——一个人可以完全支配自己的财富，不需要任何人许可。他们自己，一分钱没有拿到。
这种自由，是数学对人类最被低估的馈赠之一。我从这份馈赠里拿走了很多。设立这个奖，首先是还债。

三
诺贝尔奖没有数学奖。这是一百多年前的一个疏漏，也许有私人原因，也许只是没想到。
后来有了菲尔兹奖，四年一次，四十岁以下；有了阿贝尔奖，每年一次，奖励一生的成就。它们都很好，但它们的节奏，是上一个时代的节奏。
数学界其实有过另一种奖。Erdős一辈子给问题标价，从二十五美元到一万美元，谁解出来，他就开一张支票。很多人把支票裱在墙上，一辈子没有兑现。他1996年去世，之后那种支票开得越来越少。
而数学正在进入一个不同的时代。人工智能做不了实验，但它能推导；人工智能很难替物理学家造一台对撞机，但它可以替数学家试一万条路。今天一个猜想从提出到解决，可能是几个月，也可能是几天。一个四年颁一次的奖，面对这样的速度，像一座四年敲一次的钟，挂在一个以天计时的时代里。

四
所以孙宇晨奖的规则很简单。
奖跟着题目走，不跟着人走。不等年会，不等提名，不等年龄。
每道题，两栏署名。一栏记证明者，一栏记形式化者，把证明搬进机器的那个人。两栏可以是同一个人，也可以隔着半个地球互不相识。人可以，AI可以，人用AI也可以，哪一栏我都不关心物种。同一个名字可以一次又一次出现，出现在哪一栏都行。
钱只有一个触发器：机器把证明从第一行核到最后一行，一步不差。通过之后，两栏中的名单就是这道题的奖金所有者。这个标准不是我发明的。Scholze把自己最重要的定理挂出来，请人搬进机器；费马大定理，此刻正被人一行一行往里搬。
机器核过之前，人类的证明也不白做。数学界接受了，名字先挂上，钱一分不动，状态栏写着：已证明，待形式化。
解题那一栏的钱，只付给上架之后才被解决的题。上架时已经解决的，证明者的名字照记，钱只付给把它搬进机器的人。这个奖记录它设立之后发生的事，不给数学史补发奖金。
分工是干净的：名字归数学界，钱归机器，出资人两边都不沾。人的判断只剩一件事，确认写进机器的那道题，就是那道题。
还剩最后一件我说了算的事：题单。哪道题上架，开什么价，由我签字。Erdős的支票，价码也是他自己写的，这里不装例外。但货架一旦挂出，就锁死：题只加不减，钱只兑不退，包括我在内，谁也改不动。写错的题，照付，然后重挂。
我的品味，全部花在这一件事上。定价之外，验证、发钱、挂名，我一票都没有。
结果说了算。

五
这套规则里，我最喜欢的是一个"等"字。
一道题被解决、被数学界接受之后，钱不马上动。证明者的名字先挂上，形式化那一栏空着，状态栏写着：已证明，待形式化。谁把这份证明搬进机器，机器核过，空栏落上名字，钱的归属之旅也在那一刻启动。
在别的奖里，等是迟滞，是流程，是必要之恶。在这里，等本身是一份清单。
Erdős的支票，很多人裱在墙上，一辈子没有兑现。裱起来的钱朝后看，是纪念；挂在链上的钱朝前看，是召集。空在那里的一栏，等于对全世界说：这里有一份活，有价。
于是这份题单同时长出另一个东西：一张公开的地图，标着人类已经认下、机器还没有认下的一切。这张图今天并不存在。它只有碎片，散在几处，从来没有统一过，更从来没有带过价。
形式化的人从来不缺热情，缺的是一张带价码的施工图。谁去填那个空，谁拿钱。从今往后，把长证明搬进机器，热情还是他们的，账单归我。

quoted_text:
Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: https://t.co/eoLGVY8yad

Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

The reality is:

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

- Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well.

Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us. I'm proud of the security foundations we've built.

- Engaging independent evaluators and advisors is industry best practice. MSL already does this today in several areas because it helps produce better work. Other labs can just do this too. In general, it would be helpful for there to be a larger and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators.

- Committing the significant majority of compute towards serving people rather than racing towards recursive self-improvement is one of the best ways to ensure we develop this technology safely. Meta has made this commitment and other labs can do this as well.

I believe the key to building a positive future for everyone is maintaining the right balance of power. This is within our power to do.

Let’s all take a moment to actually watch this exchange in full, where the VP was specifically asked about Israel.  

Q: JD, before we wrap here, I want to ask you another hard question. This one about our relationship with the state of Israel and the president's relationship with Bibi Netanyahu. Many people in the Republican Party, MAGA, are now moving to a new party: America first, America only. There's a rise in anti-Semitism, and there's a persistent belief amongst a lot of the people on the right that maybe our foreign policy is too influenced by the state of Israel or Bibi Netanyahu. Can you take us into the relationship right now, where it stands, and the you know the administration's position on collaborating with Israel on a lot of these military activities.

VP: Yeah, you know what the president has said, Jason, is obviously Israel has been an important partner when it comes to military technology, when it comes to intelligence sharing, but also sometimes the United States doesn't always agree with Israel, and I think that more than frankly any president in the last 40 years, he has shown a willingness to actually part ways with Bibi Netanyahu when he feels like the interests of the American people are different from the interests of of the government of Israel.

And I find it a little ironic, Jason, that you have Democrats criticizing Donald Trump for his relationship with Bibi when Donald Trump is the one president of the last 40 years who's been willing to say, you know what, yeah, Bibi is a good partner, but also Bibi and I have a different opinion on this, or Bibi's wrong about this, or maybe Bibi's right about this from the perspective of Israel. But the American people need us to go in a different direction. So I just think that rooting this relationship, like all relationships, in America's interest is the way to actually have a rational conversation here.

Because when you're talking about whether a given policy is in America's interest, and you keep yourself laser focused on that, I think that's how you make sure that the American people know that you're fighting for them. But I also think that it allows us to actually rationally focus and force ourselves to have a conversation about when something that maybe sounded good or maybe has become a cliche or a slogan for the past 20 or 30 years. Well, maybe we have to do something different now, and I think that that's how we have to approach not just this relationship but all relationships.

By the way, you you see a similar pushback when the president makes the argument that he's made about NATO, which is yes, obviously a lot of important relationships, a lot of important partnerships in NATO, but that doesn't mean that we're going to completely make our European foreign policy subservient to NATO in the same way that we cannot let our Middle Eastern foreign policy be subservient to the state of Israel. We're going to work with people when we work with them. We're going to disagree when we disagree, and we're going to pursue America's interests. That's the only way to have a rational foreign policy.

Twenty-one of the world's largest banks are building a dollar stablecoin that, by law, cannot pay its holders a cent, and that ban is a reason they want to build it.

On September 1, a consortium including @GoldmanSachs, @Citi, @BankofAmerica, @DeutscheBank, @UBS, and MUFG confirmed plans to form a company this year and bring a GENIUS Act-compliant USD stablecoin to market in H1 2027, on public chains.

Under GENIUS, a payment stablecoin issuer cannot pass any yield to holders.

For a crypto-native issuer that is a handicap; for these banks it removes the one axis where a newcomer could undercut them and moves the contest to settlement and distribution, where incumbents already win.

> 21 banks, including Goldman, Citi, BofA, Deutsche, UBS, MUFG
> USD token targeted for H1 2027, on public blockchains
> GENIUS bars issuers from paying any yield to holders
> USDT and USDC still hold ~85% of a ~$303B stablecoin market . . .

The ban relocates the demand for yield rather than removing it. The reserve income these tokens throw off goes to the issuer, not the holder, so every dollar parked in one is a dollar whose owner still wants a return and has to earn it somewhere the token itself cannot provide.

The larger this non-yielding money layer grows, the larger the pool of capital sitting on top of it with nowhere to compound.

That capital looks for a compliant, risk-managed place to turn a parked balance into real return, a different job from issuing the dollar and a harder one than settling it.

One caveat: a three-party consortium structure may route yield indirectly, and regulators have moved to treat those arrangements as breaking the rule, so the line is not yet settled.

But the token itself still pays its holder nothing.

Smart money is watching where the yield on all this parked stablecoin ends up, because a bigger layer of money that cannot earn is the clearest signal yet of demand for the layer that makes it earn.

Source in 🧵

text:
After many months of research and consideration, $CODEC is once again my highest conviction trade.

My bullishness for robotics never left, however the environment clearly wasn’t favourable and products were still too immature to have a real impact on development.

So why the sudden change of mind? What’s so interesting that’s brought me back?

Firstly, this wasn’t an overnight decision. Around 3 months ago I was coming back from a trading hiatus, since my read on the market wasn’t great, a protocol I have to better my edge is reading as much non crypto related material as possible. This is my favourite tool in the arsenal to respark my curiosity, which is one of, if not the most valuable trait when becoming interested in your craft again.

By reading about non crypto related sectors, it helps open my mind on potential possibilities through breaking a close minded state. You realise how much opportunity, innovation and capital flows through society as a whole. As you can probably guess, one of these topics was related to robotics.

In my telegram channel, I spoke about the introduction of World Action Models (WAM) and Egoscale + Scaling Laws. Very quickly I realized how much the space had progressed over just a 6-9 month period. A complete step change had been made across nearly every vertical, many of the theses I had a year ago have arrived and are showing rapid improvement. Since then, it’s been the core narrative sitting in the back of my mind that I haven’t been able to shake.

I’ll try to keep the key points short as each of them deserves their own article, which I’ll hopefully write in the near future.

1. World Action Models (WAM) - a new architecture which builds on VLA’s/VLM’s by adding prediction. Instead of only choosing an action, they try to predict how the scene will change after that action. Data collection through teleoperation is largely inefficient, humanized sensors are massively growing and companies adjacent to them. Nvidia defines them as models that predict future world states and actions. DreamZero see’s WAMs as a way to learn physical dynamics and generalize to unseen motions where standard VLAs can struggle. Robotics is moving from task specific policies toward general purpose physical intelligence.

2. EgoScale and Scaling Laws - trained a VLA on 20k hours of action labeled egocentric human video, found a log linear scaling law between human data scale and validation loss, showed that validation loss strongly tracks downstream robot performance and reported a 54% average robot success improvement over no pretraining on a 22 DoF dexterous hand. This has been proof that dexterity can improve with better and more data.

3. In context learning - In context learning lets models learn new tasks from examples instead of by changing weights. This is not the same as permanently learning a skill. The robot changes its behavior while the demonstration is in context, but its model weights are not updated. So in the next session, that skill is gone. Generalist AI’s GEN 1.5 shows that a robot can take a short demo video as a “prompt” and immediately perform the task. In trials on simple tasks, it learned from just one demonstration with no extra training. This proof of concept suggests robot skills can be transferred by demonstration much as GPT learns from text prompts, although this is only for short horizon context, not long tasks. Prompted skills aren’t as good as fine tuned ones. Nevertheless it’s a massive progression.

4. Simulations - They’ll never capture everything that happens in the real world, but what they do give us is access to information that is difficult to get from videos alone such as the exact position of objects, contact points, forces, and robot movements. That makes simulation a useful complement to real world data. Codec (SimArena) can help by providing realistic, calibrated simulations and task setups that match the robot being used. This gives the model more examples to learn from and helps it make better predictions

5. Systems - As tooling, benchmarking, authoring layer, system ID etc become more advanced, robotics slowly becomes a compute problem. Different physical robots and even two nominally identical copies do not behave identically. Simulation tooling can’t accurately correlate between foundation models. System ID is the missing layer and where simulation tooling like Codec will be able to abstract calibrations, giving more confidence for deploying in reality.

So what specific tasks am I focused on?

- Publicising robotics research and being in the weeds for every new innovation that’s coming out on a daily basis

- Positioning Codec’s marketing so it fully captures how the architecture is aligned with industry standards and future bottlenecks

- Help @unmoyai put his big brain thoughts onto this app as there’s very few people with his technical knowledge + experience

- Simplify and point readers of my page in the right direction, the entire sector has multiplied. There’s so many new sub fields and interesting experiments happening that are often complex and hard to keep track of

- Bullposting

I’ll address the elephant in the room and explain why I left unannounced previously, which I want to apologise for.

With start ups and especially in crypto, small decisions make a massive difference. Everything is about attention to detail and rapid execution. I was extremely hands on with product positioning, marketing, business analysis etc alongside my own bullposting and trading, which was a position I was comfortable to be in, since I’ve scaled multiple companies before.

Due to being so hands on, I was very passionate and strong minded on certain decisions, I treated the product like it was my own and even wrote a 30 page product and business analysis on every vertical. At some stage myself and the team had weak communication while trying to move at a high growth start up pace. This eventually led to myself being frustrated as there was too many chefs in the kitchen and conflict from multiple marketing heads.

So with this conflict, I silently stepped away as I had too much respect for the @codecopenflow team, @0xdetweiler and everyone else involved behind the scenes who put so much effort in. Looking back, did I handle the situation well? Probably not, but when I become passionate on my work I treat it like life or death. With my departure I gave a list of items which needed to be improved from my perspective regarding processes, operations, positioning and overall structure. I can confidently say these have greatly improved and with my inputs I should be able to help put the icing on the cake.

Due to past experiences, I know there will be some people uncertain of my commitment. To help with my transparency towards being dedicated for the long term, you’ll be able to watch my Fomo account.

I wished I could have made this post when the price was ranging at 2-3 mil. However this wasn’t a decision I took lightly and I wasn’t risking my reputation, I’ve spent over 2 months going back and forth with the team making sure I understand every vertical to a tea. This wasn’t a decision I was going to make without seeing a clear long term roadmap that matches how I see the robotics industry evolving.

As the terminator once said: “I’m back”

Codec coded.

text:
Interesting paper: a geometric attack breaks two direct post-quantum lattice-based authenticated key exchange constructions through reconciliation-signal leakage with key recovery. 
Doesn't affect the standard ML-KEM, but interesting in an architectural way. The hardness of underlying assumption doesn't automatically imply security of the protocol built around it. Information leaked by reconciliation step here became the attack surface.
Post-quantum migration is not just about choosing a new assumption to replace elliptic-curves. The protocol constructions are different, and practical approaches need to be relearned and account for every new way through which the protocol reveals information about the secret.

早期Alpha项目推荐——<HyperLeaf @HyperLeafHQ >

HyperLeaf 是一个部署在 HyperEVM（Hyperliquid 的 EVM 链）上的早期 DeFi 基础设施项目。

核心功能：
把别的链上能生息、但锁定的仓位，包装成 HyperEVM 上的一张可转让收据，让这个仓位能在 HyperEVM 上被拿去交易或组合

具体步骤：
- Deposit：向协议中deposit对应资产，协议按listing铸造对应的Leaf

- 获取收益: 收益来自原协议本身的排放，已实现收益中99%留给持有人，协议收取1%

- Exit：
能赎回的（L 类）：烧 Leaf，unwrap 回原资产，例如 hQUID、hAVNT、hgSOON
不能赎回的（C1 / sell-only）：协议不承诺兑付，只能去 Leaf Market 找买家，例如 hNEST、BLUAI4Y

已上线资产：
- hNEST
- hQUID
- hAVNT
- BLUAI4Y
- hgSOON

注：
- 未经外部人工审计，早期、小额度、可暂停
- sell-only 的 Leaf 没有官方赎回
- Leaf 不是原项目官方代币

text:
In LSC, contract interfaces encode behavior, not just method shapes.

Stating that your contract `implements IERC20` in Solidity only forces you to expose the methods defined by the interface. The expected behavior is only a convention and Solidity can not enforce it.

Stating `implements IERC20` in LSC means that you have a proof obligation to show that your contract behaves like an ERC-20 token.

On the caller side, Solidity has no way to check whether your use of an external address is sound. Best you can do is mock, e2e test or fork test.

In LSC, using `Ref (IERC20 asset0)` means that your proofs can rely on this behavior when proving your own theorems. It also means that your contract is compatible with any ERC-20, including rebasing and fee-on-transfer tokens. Use `Ref (IERC20.Exact asset0)` if that is not the case.

It's still EVM though, behavior is not on chain so it's only declarative at construction.

text:
美国 Bitcoin 战略储备法案推进

美国 bitcoin:native 战略储备法案 H.R.8957 将在9月16日（北京时间9月17日）接受众议院金融服务委员会审议。这个审议通过的概率还是挺高的。

不过虽然法案已经有23名共同提案人，也有民主党议员参与推动，但委员会通过以后，还需要众议院全院和参议院通过，再交总统签署。参议院如果遭遇阻挠，通常需要60票才能结束辩论（就和刚刚结束的清晰法案一样），目前还看不到足够的证据说明这些票已经凑齐。

这份法案对新增买币的要求也比较克制。第九条要求财政部和商务部在法案生效后180天内，研究如何在不增加财政负担的情况下增持 BTC，没有确定购买数量和买入时间。

9月14日提交的替代修正案明确这是一条不授权为买币新增借款、征税或赤字支出。可以理解为卖出罚没的其它资产来购买 BTC ，大概是这样，当然还有其它的解释原因。

对于 BTC 来说，如果法案最终通过，肯定是 100% 的利好，全球第一次有发达国家把 Bitcoin 做过国家级战略储备，但实际上的可行性还不知道，主要还是要看民主党议员的支持情况。

 @Gate Crypto、美股、港股、韩股、黄金、CFD、预测市场一站交易
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
今天凌晨给 Clarity Act 投反对票的密歇根州参议员的自白，顺便说一下，这位是民主党。

她反对这版 CLARITY 法案，主要有三个原因：

1. 对公职人员利益冲突的限制太弱。 她认为法案没有充分约束总统、家属和内阁成员利用加密业务获利。并强调这类限制也应适用于未来的民主党官员。

2. 反洗钱和国家安全措施不足。 她认为还需要加强阻断非法资金的工具，防止恐怖组织，以及朝鲜、伊朗等国家利用加密渠道融资。

3. 监管机构缺乏执行能力。 包括 CFTC 在内的机构，目前监管能力和人员配置不足，难以有效落实法案。

不过她也同时表示，支持美国在加密创新中保持领先，也认可法案中的部分跨党派条款，愿意继续参与修改和推进。

这就说明起码还是有部分的民主党议员是愿意支持加密货币在美国的发展，而我看了几个发言人，最重要的说法都是在第一条。

And the prize is control over largest economy in the world, the most influential companies in the world, and the most powerful military ever built.

The groups that either started this game or recognized it early on are winning with remarkable success. They've now learned the tricks, skills, and strategies necessary to continue winning, especially as long as they go largely unopposed.

Some groups are so lost or blind to the game, that they continue to score for other teams, or injure their own teammates in bumbling incompetence, not realizing they're on the field.

I hate the game, because the culture my great grandkids will grow up in is now part of a pot to be won, but I have no hope that the game itself will stop.

So instead of hating the other teams and they're players (a losing strategy), the only thing we can do is start competing.

New on Yukon: the Quantum Safe Bitcoin Challenge, with @StarkWareLtd.

https://t.co/whr53f3o55

On August 26 the first quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction landed on mainnet. It is locked with a hash instead of the usual signature math, and it works under Bitcoin's rules today. No soft fork.

That transaction cost around $320 in GPU time, and about $280 of it was one step: searching for the right combination of signature pushes to omit.

That step is the challenge. Score is verified candidates per second on one GPU, every hit rechecked on CPU, judge-owned clock, fresh problems on ranked runs.

Speed up the search and almost the entire cost comes down with it.

Antibiotic-depleted rats given gut microbiota pooled from 3 severely depressed men developed anhedonia and anxiety-like behavior. The healthy-donor group showed no such change.

Kynurenine/tryptophan ratio rose too (28 rats).
https://t.co/Z9vewx1NNu
author: ResearchHub
quoted_text:
Si coges bacterias intestinales de personas con depresión y las introduces en ratas, esas ratas se deprimen.

En este estudio se comparó la microbiota de personas con depresión y de personas sanas. En las que estaban deprimidas, el ecosistema intestinal era más pobre y menos diverso. También había un perfil inflamatorio más alto —más IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α y proteína C reactiva—, una mayor producción de cortisol y un desvío del triptófano hacia la vía de la quinurenina: un mayor ratio quinurenina/triptófano.

Para comprobar si eso podía tener un efecto causal, se transfirió esa microbiota a ratas cuya microbiota intestinal había sido deplecionada. Unas recibieron la de personas deprimidas y otras, como control, la de personas sanas. Solo las primeras desarrollaron anhedonia (menos interés por las recompensas) y conducta de tipo ansioso. En ellas también subió la quinurenina plasmática y el ratio quinurenina/triptófano, se alargó el tránsito intestinal y la proteína C reactiva tendió a elevarse.

author: chadwahl
quoted_text:
Apache Iceberg is now generally available in Palantir AIP.

Sovereignty at all levels of the stack.

Customers can now use an open, interoperable table format alongside the capabilities required to operate critical data: pipeline building, governance, security, lineage, and Ontology.

The full open standard, not some Palantir variant of it...... THE FULL OPEN STANDARD.

Managed Iceberg tables and Palantir’s Iceberg REST catalog are GA on standard Foundry enterprise environments. Tables can be stored in Palantir managed storage or a customer-provided bucket.

This means one bucket (yours, ours or theirs), one iceberg file, Palantir and your other Iceberg enabled systems working on the same physical file. Zero Data Copy.

Teams can build pipelines, perform row-level updates and changelog processing, create Ontology object types backed by Iceberg, analyze tables in with SQL, python or connect external tools directly to the catalog. Completely open.

Adopting and supporting an open standard means more than consuming it.

Our FDEs have also contributed back to the Iceberg standard to enable features we had built in Foundry but now is available as part of the standard for all, just a few examples:

- Table encryption in iceberg-rust https://t.co/r1AYyb4KAM

- Incremental append scans, schema evolution, and other Iceberg features in Polars https://t.co/XZrVhJVRCA
